sentences.zh: 李華李華，字遐叔，趙州贊皇人。

translations.literal: Li Hua Li Hua, style name Xiashu, was a man of Zanhuang in Zhao Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Li Hua, courtesy name Xiashu, was a native of Zanhuang in Zhao Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 曾祖太沖，名冠宗族間，鄕人語曰：「太沖無兄。」

translations.literal: His great-grandfather Taichong's fame topped the clan; villagers said, "Taichong has no elder brother."
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandfather Taichong was foremost in reputation within the clan; neighbors used to say, "Among brothers, none ranks above Taichong.

sentences.zh: 太宗時，擢祠部郎中。

translations.literal: In Emperor Taizong's time he was promoted to Director in the Ministry of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: During the reign of Emperor Taizong, he was promoted to Director in the Ministry of Rites.

sentences.zh: 華少曠達，外若坦蕩，内謹重，尚然許，毎慕汲黯爲人。

translations.literal: Hua in youth was broad and open; outwardly he seemed free and easy, inwardly careful and weighty; he esteemed Ran Kui and Xu You and always admired Ji An's conduct.
translations.idiomatic: In his youth Hua was free-spirited and open-minded: outwardly he seemed easygoing, yet inwardly he was careful and earnest. He admired Ran Kui and Xu You and always took Ji An as his model.

sentences.zh: 累中進士、宏辭科。

translations.literal: He repeatedly passed the jinshi and the hongci examinations.
translations.idiomatic: He passed both the jinshi examination and the hongci literary examination.

sentences.zh: 天寶十一載，遷監察御史。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year of Tianbao he was transferred to Investigating Censor.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year of the Tianbao era (752), he was appointed Investigating Censor.

sentences.zh: 宰相楊國忠支婭所在橫猾，華出使，劾按不橈，州縣肅然。

translations.literal: Wherever the collateral kin of the chief minister Yang Guozhong were, they were overbearing and crafty; Hua went out on missions, investigated and pressed without bending, and prefectures and counties became orderly.
translations.idiomatic: Wherever the collateral branches of Chief Minister Yang Guozhong's family were posted, they acted with domineering violence and guile. When Hua went out on inspection tours, he investigated them without yielding, and the prefectures and counties became orderly at once.

sentences.zh: 爲權幸見疾，徙右補闕。

translations.literal: The powerful and favored came to resent him, and he was moved to Right Remonstrator.
translations.idiomatic: Those in power came to resent him, and he was transferred to the post of Right Remonstrator.

sentences.zh: 安祿山反，上誅守之策，皆留不服。

translations.literal: When An Lushan rebelled, he submitted strategies for defense to the throne; all were kept on file and not adopted.
translations.idiomatic: When An Lushan rose in rebellion, he submitted plans for defending the realm to the emperor, but every proposal was filed away and left unimplemented.

sentences.zh: 玄宗入蜀，百官解竄，華母在鄴，欲間行輦母以逃，爲盜所得，偽署鳳閣舍人。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xuanzong entered Shu, officials scattered in flight; Hua's mother was at Ye. He wished to slip away on foot to escort his mother in flight, but was seized by bandits and falsely appointed Gentleman Attendant at the Phoenix Pavilion.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xuanzong fled into Shu, the officials scattered in panic. Hua's mother was at Ye, and he tried to slip away on foot to escort her to safety, but was seized by bandits and given a false appointment as Gentleman Attendant at the Phoenix Pavilion.

sentences.zh: 賊平，貶杭州司戸參軍。

translations.literal: When the rebels were pacified, he was demoted to Registrar in Hangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: After the rebellion was suppressed, he was demoted to Registrar in Hangzhou.

sentences.zh: 華自傷踐危亂，不能完節，又不能安親，欲終養而母亡，遂屛居江南。

translations.literal: Hua grieved that he had passed through peril and disorder without preserving his integrity and could not keep his parent secure; he wished to support his mother to the end, but she died, and he then withdrew to live in seclusion south of the Yangtze.
translations.idiomatic: Hua grieved that he had lived through chaos without preserving his integrity and had failed to keep his mother safe. He had hoped to support her in her old age, but she died, and he withdrew to live in seclusion in the south.

sentences.zh: 上元中，以左補闕、司封員外郎召之。

translations.literal: In the Shangyuan era he was summoned as Left Remonstrator and an outer member of the Ministry of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: During the Shangyuan era, he was summoned back as Left Remonstrator and Outer Member of the Ministry of Rites.

sentences.zh: 華喟然曰：「烏有隳節危親，欲荷天子寵乎？」

translations.literal: Hua sighed and said, "How could one who has broken his integrity and endangered his kin hope to bear the Son of Heaven's favor?"
translations.idiomatic: Hua sighed and said, "How could someone who has compromised his integrity and put his family in peril still hope to accept the emperor's favor?

sentences.zh: 稱疾不拜。

translations.literal: He pleaded illness and did not take office.
translations.idiomatic: He pleaded illness and refused the appointment.

sentences.zh: 李峴領選江南，表置幕府，擢檢校吏部員外郎。

translations.literal: Li Xian, overseeing selection in the south, memorialized to place him in his staff and promoted him to Acting Outer Member of the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Xian oversaw official selection in the south, he recommended Hua for his staff and promoted him to Acting Outer Member of the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 苦風痹，去官，客隱山陽，勒子弟力農，安於窮槁。

translations.literal: Afflicted with wind paralysis, he left office, lodged in seclusion at Shanyang, urged his sons and younger kin to labor at farming, and was content in poverty.
translations.idiomatic: Tormented by rheumatism, he resigned his post, lived as a guest-recluse at Shanyang, urged his sons and nephews to work the fields, and was content in poverty.

sentences.zh: 晩事浮圖法，不甚著書，惟天下士大夫家傳、墓版及州縣碑頌，時時齎金帛往請，乃強爲應。

translations.literal: In his later years he devoted himself to Buddhist law, did not write much, and only when gentlemen throughout the realm brought gold and silk to request family histories, tomb inscriptions, or local stele eulogies would he force himself to comply.
translations.idiomatic: In his later years he devoted himself to Buddhism and wrote little. Only when scholars from across the realm came with gold and silk to request family histories, tomb inscriptions, or local commemorative steles would he reluctantly oblige.

sentences.zh: 大暦初，卒。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Dali era he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died early in the Dali era.

sentences.zh: 初，華作《含元殿賦》成，以示蕭穎士，穎士曰：「《景福》之上，《靈光》之下。」

translations.literal: Earlier, when Hua finished his "Rhapsody on the Hall of Universal Origin" and showed it to Xiao Yingshi, Yingshi said, "Above the Jingfu fu, below the Lingguang fu."
translations.idiomatic: When Hua first completed his "Rhapsody on the Hall of Universal Origin" and showed it to Xiao Yingshi, Yingshi said, "It ranks above the Jingfu Rhapsody but below the Lingguang Rhapsody.

sentences.zh: 華文辭綿麗，少宏傑氣，穎士健爽自肆，時謂不及穎士，而華自疑過之。

translations.literal: Hua's prose was lush and fine but lacked bold grandeur; Yingshi was vigorous, forthright, and unrestrained. The age said Hua did not match Yingshi, yet Hua himself suspected he surpassed him.
translations.idiomatic: Hua's writing was lush and refined but lacked bold grandeur, whereas Yingshi was vigorous, forthright, and unrestrained. People of the time said Hua did not equal Yingshi, yet Hua himself suspected he was the better writer.

sentences.zh: 因著《吊古戰塲文》，極思研扌隺，已成，汙爲故書，雜置梵書之庋。

translations.literal: He therefore wrote "Elegy for an Ancient Battlefield," polishing it with utmost thought. When it was done, he smeared it to look like an old text and mixed it among shelves of Buddhist books.
translations.idiomatic: He therefore wrote his "Elegy for an Ancient Battlefield," refining it with the utmost care. When it was finished, he stained the manuscript to make it look ancient and slipped it among the shelves of Buddhist scriptures.

sentences.zh: 它日，與穎士讀之，稱工，華問：「今誰可及？」

translations.literal: Another day he read it with Yingshi, who praised its craft. Hua asked, "Who today could match it?"
translations.idiomatic: On another day he read it with Yingshi, who praised its craftsmanship. Hua asked, "Who alive today could equal it?

sentences.zh: 穎士曰：「君加精思，便能至矣。」

translations.literal: Yingshi said, "If you refine your thought further, you can reach that level."
translations.idiomatic: Yingshi replied, "If you refine your thinking a little more, you can reach that level yourself."

sentences.zh: 華愕然而服。

translations.literal: Hua was startled and submitted.
translations.idiomatic: Hua was startled—and convinced.

sentences.zh: 華愛獎士類，名隨以重，若獨孤及、韓雲卿、韓會、李紓、柳識、崔祐甫、皇甫冉、謝良弼、硃巨川，後至執政顯官。

translations.literal: Hua loved to encourage men of talent, and his fame grew weighty with it. Such men as Dugu Ji, Han Yunqing, Han Hui, Li Shu, Liu Shi, Cui Youfu, Huangfu Ran, Xie Liangbi, and Zhu Juchuan later reached high office and prominence.
translations.idiomatic: Hua loved to encourage talented men, and his reputation grew accordingly. Men such as Dugu Ji, Han Yunqing, Han Hui, Li Shu, Liu Shi, Cui Youfu, Huangfu Ran, Xie Liangbi, and Zhu Juchuan later rose to high office.

sentences.zh: 華觸禍銜悔，及爲元德秀、權皋銘、《四皓贊》，稱道深婉，讀者憐其志。

translations.literal: Hua met disaster and bore regret; when he wrote inscriptions for Yuan Dexiu and Quan Gao and his "Encomium on the Four Hoary Heads," his praise was deep and subtle, and readers pitied his intent.
translations.idiomatic: After meeting disaster and living with regret, the inscriptions he wrote for Yuan Dexiu and Quan Gao and his "Encomium on the Four Hoary Heads" were deep and subtle in praise; readers pitied the spirit behind them.

sentences.zh: 宗子翰，從子觀，皆有名。

translations.literal: His clansman son Han and his nephew son Guan were both famed.
translations.idiomatic: His clansman Han and his nephew Guan were both well known.

sentences.zh: 子 翰翰擢進士第，調衞尉。

translations.literal: Son Han: Han passed the jinshi and was assigned to the Court of the Imperial Stud.
translations.idiomatic: Han passed the jinshi examination and was appointed to the Court of the Imperial Stud.

sentences.zh: 天寶末，房琯、韋陟倶薦爲史官，宰相不肯擬。

translations.literal: At the end of Tianbao, Fang Guan and Wei Zhi both recommended him as historiographer, but the chief minister would not draft the appointment.
translations.idiomatic: Near the end of the Tianbao era, Fang Guan and Wei Zhi both recommended him for a historiographer post, but the chief minister refused to draft the appointment.

sentences.zh: 翰所善張巡死節睢陽，人媢其功，以爲降賊，肅宗未及知。

translations.literal: Zhang Xun, whom Han favored, died loyal at Suiyang; people envied his merit and said he had surrendered to the rebels, and Emperor Suzong had not yet learned the truth.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Xun, whom Han admired, had died defending Suiyang to the last, yet envious men denied his achievement and claimed he had surrendered to the rebels—a charge Emperor Suzong had not yet had the chance to refute.

sentences.zh: 翰傳巡功狀，表上之，曰：

translations.literal: Han circulated an account of Xun's achievements and memorialized it to the throne, saying:
translations.idiomatic: Han drew up an account of Zhang Xun's achievements and submitted it in a memorial, saying:

sentences.zh: 「臣聞聖主褒死難之士，養死事之孤，或親推轜車，或追建邑封，厚死以慰生，撫存以答亡，君不遺於臣，臣亦不背其君也。

translations.literal: "Your servant has heard that a sage ruler honors men who die in hardship, nurtures the orphans of those who died in service, sometimes personally pushes the funeral cart, sometimes posthumously establishes fiefs—enriching the dead to comfort the living, cherishing the living to answer the dead. The ruler does not abandon his minister; the minister does not betray his ruler.
translations.idiomatic: "Your servant has heard that a sage ruler honors those who die in hardship and cares for the orphans of men who died in his service—sometimes personally attending the funeral cart, sometimes granting posthumous fiefs. He enriches the dead to comfort the living and cherishes the living to answer the dead. When the ruler does not abandon his minister, the minister does not betray his ruler.

sentences.zh: 自逆胡構亂，據雒陽，引幽、朔以呑河南，故御史中丞、贈揚州大都督張巡，忠誼奮發，率烏合，守雍丘，潰賊心腹。

translations.literal: Since the rebel barbarian raised disorder, seized Luoyang, and drew You and Shuo to swallow Henan, the former Vice Censor-in-Chief, posthumously Grand Governor of Yangzhou, Zhang Xun, loyal and ardent, led a rabble host, held Yongqiu, and shattered the rebels' heartland.
translations.idiomatic: Since the rebel chieftain raised rebellion, seized Luoyang, and drew the armies of You and Shuo to overrun Henan, Zhang Xun—formerly Vice Censor-in-Chief, posthumously honored as Grand Governor of Yangzhou—rose in loyal fervor, led a hastily gathered force, held Yongqiu, and struck at the rebels' heartland.

sentences.zh: 及魯炅棄甲宛、葉，哥舒翰敗績潼關，賊送盜神器，鴟峙二京，南臨漢、江，西逼岐、雍，群帥列城，望風出奔，巡守孤城不爲卻。

translations.literal: When Lu Ling abandoned arms at Wan and Ye and Geshu Han was defeated at Tong Pass, the rebels pressed on to seize the sacred vessel, stood like owls over the two capitals, looked south on the Han and Yangtze, pressed west on Qi and Yong—commanders in walled cities fled at the wind—yet Xun held his lone city and did not yield.
translations.idiomatic: When Lu Ling threw away his armor at Wan and Ye and Geshu Han was routed at Tong Pass, the rebels pressed forward to seize the imperial regalia, perched like owls over the two capitals, threatened the Han and Yangtze to the south and Qi and Yong to the west, and commanders in walled cities fled at the mere rumor of their approach—yet Zhang Xun held his isolated city and would not retreat.

sentences.zh: 賊欲繞出巡後以擾江淮，巡退軍睢陽，扼東南咽領。

translations.literal: The rebels wished to circle behind Xun to harry the Jiang-Huai region; Xun withdrew his army to Suiyang and choked the throat of the southeast.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels wished to slip behind Zhang Xun to ravage the Jiang-Huai region, so he withdrew his army to Suiyang and blocked the strategic throat of the southeast.

sentences.zh: 自春訖冬，大戰數十，小戰數百，以弱制強，出奇無窮，殺馘凶醜凡十余萬，賊不敢越睢陽取江淮，江淮以完，巡之力也。

translations.literal: From spring through winter he fought great battles by the tens and small battles by the hundreds, used the weak to control the strong, deployed endless stratagems, and killed more than a hundred thousand fierce enemies; the rebels dared not cross Suiyang to take the Jiang-Huai, and the Jiang-Huai remained intact—this was Xun's power.
translations.idiomatic: From spring through winter he fought dozens of major engagements and hundreds of lesser ones, used the weak to overcome the strong, and deployed endless stratagems, killing more than a hundred thousand of the enemy. The rebels dared not pass Suiyang to seize the Jiang-Huai, and the Jiang-Huai remained intact—this was Zhang Xun's achievement.

sentences.zh: 城孤糧盡，外救不至，猶奮羸起病，摧鋒陷堅，三軍啖膚而食，知死不叛。

translations.literal: The city was isolated and grain exhausted; outside aid did not come, yet he still roused the feeble and sick to battle, shattered spearpoints and broke ramparts; the whole army ate flesh and knew death yet did not rebel.
translations.idiomatic: When the city stood alone and provisions were gone, with no relief from outside, he still roused the weak and sick to fight, smashed enemy lines and stormed fortifications; the whole army ate human flesh yet knew they faced death and would not defect.

sentences.zh: 城陷見執，卒無橈詞，慢叱凶徒，精貫白日，雖古忠烈無以加焉。

translations.literal: When the city fell he was seized; to the end he had no yielding words, slowly reviled the vicious band, his spirit piercing the white sun—though ancient loyal martyrs could not surpass this.
translations.idiomatic: When the city fell he was captured, yet to the end he would not yield in word, calmly reviled his captors, and his spirit shone like the sun at noon—no loyal martyr of antiquity could surpass him.

sentences.zh: 「議者罪巡以食人，愚巡以守死，臣竊痛之。

translations.literal: "Critics condemn Xun for eating men; fools condemn Xun for dying at his post—your servant privately grieves this.
translations.idiomatic: "Critics condemn Zhang Xun for cannibalism; fools condemn him for dying at his post. Your servant is deeply grieved by this.

sentences.zh: 夫忠者，臣之教；

translations.literal: Loyalty is the teaching for ministers;
translations.idiomatic: Loyalty is what a minister is taught;

sentences.zh: 恕者，法之情。

translations.literal: forgiveness is the feeling of law.
translations.idiomatic: forgiveness is the spirit of the law.

sentences.zh: 巡握節而死，非虧教也；

translations.literal: Xun grasped his tally and died—this is not a breach of teaching;
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Xun died grasping his tally of office—he did not fail in loyalty;

sentences.zh: 析骸以爨，非本情也。

translations.literal: splitting bones to cook was not his original intent.
translations.idiomatic: splitting corpses for fuel was not his original intent.

sentences.zh: 《春秋》以功覆過，《書》赦過宥刑，在《易》遏惡揚善，爲國者録用棄瑕。

translations.literal: The Spring and Autumn Annals cover faults with merit; the Documents pardon faults and spare punishment; in the Changes one checks evil and exalts good; rulers of states record merit and set aside flaws.
translations.idiomatic: The Spring and Autumn Annals cover faults with merit; the Documents pardon faults and spare punishment; the Changes teach that one should check evil and exalt good; rulers of states record merit and set aside flaws.

sentences.zh: 今者乃欲議巡之罪，是廢教絀節，不以功掩過，不以刑恕情，善可遏，惡可揚，瑕録而用棄，非所以獎人倫，明勸戒也。

translations.literal: Now to discuss Xun's crime is to abolish teaching and diminish integrity, not to cover faults with merit, not to pardon feeling with punishment—good can be checked, evil can be exalted, flaws recorded and merit discarded; this is not how to encourage human relations and clarify admonition.
translations.idiomatic: To debate Zhang Xun's crimes now would be to abandon the teaching of loyalty and diminish integrity—not to cover faults with merit, not to temper punishment with mercy, to let good be suppressed and evil exalted, to record flaws and discard merit. That is no way to encourage proper conduct or make clear what should be rewarded and what condemned.

sentences.zh: 且祿山背德，大臣將相比肩從賊，巡官不朝，宴不坐，無一伍之士，一節之權，徒奮身死節，以動義旅，不謂忠乎？

translations.literal: Moreover Lushan betrayed virtue; great ministers and generals lined up to follow the rebels. Xun did not attend court, did not sit at banquets, had not a squad of soldiers nor a tally of authority—he merely threw himself into death for integrity to stir the righteous host. Is this not called loyalty?
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, Lushan betrayed his sovereign, while great ministers and generals lined up to follow the rebels. Zhang Xun held no court office, sat at no imperial banquet, commanded not even a squad of soldiers nor wielded a tally of authority—he merely threw himself into death for the sake of integrity to stir the righteous armies. Is this not loyalty?

sentences.zh: 以數千卒橫挫賊鋒，若無巡則無睢陽，無睢陽則無江淮。

translations.literal: With a few thousand soldiers he bluntly checked the rebels' spearpoint; without Xun there would be no Suiyang, without Suiyang no Jiang-Huai.
translations.idiomatic: With only a few thousand men he blocked the rebels' advance at the spearpoint; without Zhang Xun there would have been no Suiyang, and without Suiyang there would have been no Jiang-Huai.

sentences.zh: 有如賊因江淮之資，兵廣而財積，根結盤據，西向以拒，雖終殲滅，其曠日持久必矣。

translations.literal: Had the rebels drawn on the Jiang-Huai's resources, with broad armies and heaped wealth, roots intertwined and coiled, and faced west to resist, though in the end they would be destroyed, the days would surely stretch long.
translations.idiomatic: Had the rebels drawn on the resources of the Jiang-Huai, with vast armies and accumulated wealth, their power rooted deep and spread wide, and turned west to resist the throne, even if they were eventually destroyed, the war would surely have dragged on far longer.

sentences.zh: 今陝、鄢一戰，犬羊駭北，王師震其西，巡扼其東，此天使巡舉江淮以待陛下，師至而巡死，不謂功乎？

translations.literal: Now at the battles of Shan and Yan the dogs and sheep fled north in terror; the imperial army shook them in the west, Xun choked them in the east—this was Heaven making Xun raise the Jiang-Huai to await Your Majesty; the army arrived and Xun died. Is this not called merit?
translations.idiomatic: At the battles of Shan and Yan the rebels fled north in terror; the imperial army struck them in the west while Zhang Xun blocked them in the east. Was this not Heaven's design—that Zhang Xun should hold the Jiang-Huai until Your Majesty's armies arrived? The armies came, and Zhang Xun died. Is this not merit?

sentences.zh: 古者列國侵伐，猶分災救患，諸將同受國恩，奉辭伐罪，巡固守亦待外援，援不至而食盡，食盡而及人，則巡之情可求矣。

translations.literal: In antiquity when feudal states invaded one another they still shared disaster and relieved distress; the generals alike received the state's grace, received the mandate to punish crime—Xun held fast and also awaited outside aid; aid did not come and food was exhausted, food exhausted and then men were reached—then Xun's situation can be understood.
translations.idiomatic: In antiquity, when feudal states made war on one another, they still shared one another's disasters and relieved one another's distress. The generals alike received the state's favor and bore the mandate to punish crime. Zhang Xun held his ground and likewise awaited outside relief; relief did not come, provisions ran out, and only then did men become food—under such circumstances his plight can be understood.

sentences.zh: 假巡守城之初，已計食人，損數百衆以全天下，臣尚謂功過相掩，況非素志乎？

translations.literal: Suppose at the beginning of holding the city Xun had already planned to eat men and sacrifice several hundred soldiers to save the realm—your servant would still say merit and fault offset each other, how much more when it was not his original intent?
translations.idiomatic: Even if, at the very start of the siege, Zhang Xun had deliberately planned to cannibalize his troops and sacrifice several hundred lives to save the realm, your servant would still say merit and fault would offset each other—how much more so when cannibalism was never his intent?

sentences.zh: 夫子制《春秋》，明褒貶，齊桓公將封禪，略不書；

translations.literal: The Master compiled the Spring and Autumn Annals to clarify praise and blame; Duke Huan of Qi was about to perform the Feng and Shan rites—barely recorded;
translations.idiomatic: Confucius compiled the Spring and Autumn Annals to make clear praise and blame. When Duke Huan of Qi was about to perform the Feng and Shan sacrifices, the Annals barely mention it;

sentences.zh: 晉文公召王河陽，書而諱之。

translations.literal: Duke Wen of Jin summoned the king to Heyang—recorded yet euphemized.
translations.idiomatic: when Duke Wen of Jin summoned the Zhou king to Heyang, the Annals record it yet veil the offense.

sentences.zh: 巡蒼黃之罪，輕於僭禪；

translations.literal: Xun's hurried crime is lighter than usurping the sacrifices;
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Xun's desperate offense is lighter than usurping the Feng and Shan rites;

sentences.zh: 興復之功，重於糾合。

translations.literal: his merit in restoring the dynasty is heavier than gathering the lords.
translations.idiomatic: his merit in restoring the dynasty outweighs the offense of summoning the king.

sentences.zh: 「今巡子亞夫雖得官，不免饑寒，江淮既巡所保，戸口充完，宜割百戸俾食其子。

translations.literal: "Now Xun's son Yafu, though he has an office, cannot escape hunger and cold; the Jiang-Huai was what Xun protected and households remain full—a hundred households should be cut off to support his son.
translations.idiomatic: "Zhang Xun's son Yafu, though he holds an office, still suffers hunger and cold. The Jiang-Huai was what Zhang Xun preserved, and its households remain intact; a hundred households should be set aside to support his son.

sentences.zh: 且強死爲厲，有所歸則不爲災。

translations.literal: Moreover the violently dead become malign spirits; when they have a place to return they do not bring disaster.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, those who die violently may become vengeful spirits; when they have a proper resting place they do not bring calamity.

sentences.zh: 巡身首分裂，將士骸骼不掩，宜於睢陽相擇髙原，起大塚，招魂而葬，旌善之義也。

translations.literal: Xun's body was split head from trunk; officers and soldiers' bones lie uncovered—on high ground near Suiyang a great mound should be raised, souls summoned and buried; this is the meaning of honoring the good.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Xun's body was torn apart, and the bones of his officers and soldiers lie unburied. On high ground near Suiyang a great tomb should be raised, their souls summoned and laid to rest—this is how the good should be honored.

sentences.zh: 臣少與巡遊，哀巡死難，不睹休明，唯令名其榮祿也。

translations.literal: Your servant in youth traveled with Xun; he grieves Xun's death in hardship, not having seen the bright restoration, and only asks that his fair name receive honor and stipend.
translations.idiomatic: Your servant traveled with Zhang Xun in his youth and grieves that he died in hardship without living to see the restoration of peace. I ask only that his good name receive honor and reward.

sentences.zh: 若不時紀録，日月浸悠，或掩而不傳，或傳而不實，巡生死不遇，誠可悲悼。

translations.literal: If not recorded in time, as days and months lengthen, perhaps covered and not transmitted, or transmitted yet not true—Xun alive and dead would not meet favor; truly pitiable.
translations.idiomatic: If his deeds are not recorded in time, as the months and years pass his story may be buried and lost, or passed on in distorted form. That Zhang Xun should meet such neglect in life and death is truly lamentable.

sentences.zh: 謹撰傳一篇，昧死上，儻得列于史官，死骨不朽。」

translations.literal: Your servant respectfully composes one biography and, risking death, submits it; if it may be placed among the historiographers, his dead bones will not perish."
translations.idiomatic: Your servant respectfully submits this biography, risking death in doing so. If it may be entered in the official histories, his bones though dead will not perish."

sentences.zh: 帝繇是感悟，而巡大節白于世，義士多之。

translations.literal: The Emperor was thereby moved to understanding, and Xun's great integrity was clarified to the world; righteous men praised him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was moved by this, Zhang Xun's great integrity was made clear to the world, and men of principle praised him widely.

sentences.zh: 翰累遷左補闕、翰林學士。

translations.literal: Han was repeatedly promoted to Left Remonstrator and Academician of the Hanlin.
translations.idiomatic: Han rose through the ranks to Left Remonstrator and Academician of the Hanlin.

sentences.zh: 大暦中，病免，客陽翟，卒。

translations.literal: In the Dali era he resigned on grounds of illness, lodged at Yangzhai as a guest, and died.
translations.idiomatic: During the Dali era he resigned because of illness, lived as a guest at Yangzhai, and died there.

sentences.zh: 翰爲文精密而思遲，常從令皇甫曾求音樂，思涸則奏之，神逸乃屬文。

translations.literal: Han's writing was precise and his thought slow; he often had his cousin Huangfu Zeng seek out music—when thought dried up, Zeng would play, and when the spirit was eased he would compose.
translations.idiomatic: Han's prose was meticulous but came slowly. He often had his cousin Huangfu Zeng play music for him: when his thoughts ran dry, Zeng would perform, and only when his spirit was eased would he write.

sentences.zh: 族弟紓，自有傳。

translations.literal: His clansman brother Shu has his own biography.
translations.idiomatic: His clansman Li Shu has a separate biography.

sentences.zh: 從子 觀觀，字元賓。

translations.literal: Nephew son Guan: Guan, style name Yuanbin.
translations.idiomatic: His nephew Guan, courtesy name Yuanbin.

sentences.zh: 貞元中，舉進士、宏辭，連中，授太子校書郎。

translations.literal: In the Zhenyuan era he passed the jinshi and hongci in succession and was appointed Collator in the Heir Apparent's Household.
translations.idiomatic: During the Zhenyuan era he passed both the jinshi and hongci examinations in succession and was appointed Collator in the Heir Apparent's Household.

sentences.zh: 卒，年二十九。

translations.literal: He died at age twenty-nine.
translations.idiomatic: He died at the age of twenty-nine.

sentences.zh: 觀屬文，不襲沿前人，時謂與韓愈相上下。

translations.literal: Guan's compositions did not follow predecessors; the age said he matched Han Yu.
translations.idiomatic: Guan wrote without imitating earlier models, and people of the time said he was Han Yu's equal.

sentences.zh: 及觀少夭，而愈後文益工，議者以觀文未極，愈老不休，故卒擅名。

translations.literal: Guan died young, while Yu later became ever more skilled; critics held that Guan's writing had not reached its peak while Yu in old age did not rest, and so in the end Yu monopolized fame.
translations.idiomatic: Guan died young, while Han Yu's writing grew ever more accomplished with age. Critics held that Guan's art had not reached its peak, whereas Yu kept writing without cease into old age, and so in the end Han Yu alone won lasting fame.

sentences.zh: 陸希聲以爲「觀尚辭，故辭勝理；

translations.literal: Lu Xisheng held that "Guan valued rhetoric, so rhetoric surpassed reason;
translations.idiomatic: Lu Xisheng remarked, "Guan prized rhetoric, so his rhetoric surpassed his reasoning;

sentences.zh: 愈尚質，故理勝辭。

translations.literal: Yu valued substance, so reason surpassed rhetoric.
translations.idiomatic: Han Yu prized substance, so his reasoning surpassed his rhetoric.

sentences.zh: 雖愈窮老，終不能加觀之辭；

translations.literal: Though Yu grew old in poverty, in the end he could not surpass Guan's rhetoric;
translations.idiomatic: Even when Han Yu grew old and poor, he could never surpass Guan's rhetoric;

sentences.zh: 觀後愈死，亦不能逮愈之質」雲。

translations.literal: after Guan died Yu also could not match Yu's substance," he said.
translations.idiomatic: and after Guan died, Han Yu could not match Guan's substance either," he said.

sentences.zh: 孟浩然孟浩然，字浩然，襄州襄陽人。

translations.literal: Meng Haoran Meng Haoran, style name Haoran, was a man of Xiangyang in Xiang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Meng Haoran, who used his given name Haoran as his courtesy name, was a native of Xiangyang in Xiang Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 少好節義，喜振人患難，隱鹿門山。

translations.literal: In youth he loved integrity and righteousness, delighted in relieving others' distress, and lived in seclusion on Mount Lumen.
translations.idiomatic: In his youth he loved integrity and righteousness, delighted in helping others in distress, and lived in seclusion on Mount Lumen.

sentences.zh: 年四十，乃游京師。

translations.literal: At age forty he then traveled to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Only at the age of forty did he travel to the capital.

sentences.zh: 嘗於太學賦詩，一座嗟伏，無敢抗。

translations.literal: Once at the Imperial Academy he composed a poem; the whole assembly sighed in submission, none daring to contend.
translations.idiomatic: Once, when he composed a poem at the Imperial Academy, the whole assembly sighed in admiration, and none dared to compete with him.

sentences.zh: 張九齡、王維雅稱道之。

translations.literal: Zhang Jiuling and Wang Wei elegantly praised him.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Jiuling and Wang Wei spoke highly of him.

sentences.zh: 維私邀入内署，俄而玄宗至，浩然匿床下，維以實對，帝喜曰：「朕聞其人而未見也，何懼而匿？」

translations.literal: Wei privately invited him into the inner office; soon Xuanzong arrived. Haoran hid under the bed. Wei told the truth. The Emperor said with pleasure, "We have heard of this man but not seen him—why fear and hide?"
translations.idiomatic: Wang Wei once invited him privately into the inner offices of the palace. Soon Emperor Xuanzong arrived. Haoran hid under the bed. Wang Wei told the truth, and the emperor said with pleasure, "We have heard of this man but never met him—why should he fear and hide?

sentences.zh: 詔浩然出。

translations.literal: He ordered Haoran to come out.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered Haoran to come out.

sentences.zh: 帝問其詩，浩然再拜，自誦所爲，至「不才明主棄」之句，帝曰：「卿不求仕，而朕未嘗棄卿，奈何誣我？」

translations.literal: The Emperor asked about his poems. Haoran bowed twice and recited his own works. At the line "Untalented, the enlightened ruler casts me aside," the Emperor said, "You did not seek office, and We never cast you aside—why slander Us?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor asked to hear his poetry. Haoran bowed twice and recited his own works. When he reached the line "Untalented, the enlightened ruler casts me aside," the emperor said, "You never sought office, and We never cast you aside—why do you slander Us?"

sentences.zh: 因放還。

translations.literal: He therefore sent him back.
translations.idiomatic: He therefore sent him home.

sentences.zh: 採訪使韓朝宗約浩然偕至京師，欲薦諸朝。

translations.literal: The Investigating Commissioner Han Chaozong arranged for Haoran to come to the capital together and wished to recommend him to the court.
translations.idiomatic: The Investigating Commissioner Han Chaozong arranged for Haoran to travel with him to the capital, intending to recommend him at court.

sentences.zh: 會故人至，劇飲歡甚，或曰：「君與韓公有期。」

translations.literal: An old friend arrived; they drank heavily in great joy. Someone said, "You have an appointment with Master Han."
translations.idiomatic: An old friend arrived, and they drank together in high spirits. Someone said, "You have an appointment with Master Han.

sentences.zh: 浩然叱曰：「業已飲，遑恤他！」

translations.literal: Haoran rebuked them, saying, "We are already drinking—why hurry to care for anything else!"
translations.idiomatic: Haoran snapped, "We are already drinking—why should I trouble myself with anything else!"

sentences.zh: 卒不赴。

translations.literal: In the end he did not go.
translations.idiomatic: In the end he did not go.

sentences.zh: 朝宗怒，辭行，浩然不悔也。

translations.literal: Chaozong was angry and took leave to depart; Haoran did not regret it.
translations.idiomatic: Chaozong was furious and left; Haoran felt no regret.

sentences.zh: 張九齡爲荊州，辟置於府，府罷。

translations.literal: When Zhang Jiuling was at Jingzhou, he recruited him to his staff; when the prefecture was abolished, [Haoran left].
translations.idiomatic: When Zhang Jiuling served as prefect of Jingzhou, he recruited Haoran to his staff; when that office ended, Haoran left service as well.

sentences.zh: 開元末，病疽背卒。

translations.literal: At the end of Kaiyuan he died of a carbuncle on the back.
translations.idiomatic: Near the end of the Kaiyuan era he died of a carbuncle on his back.

sentences.zh: 後樊澤爲節度使，時浩然墓庳壞，符載以牋叩澤曰：「故處士孟浩然，文質傑美，殞落歳久，門裔陵遲，丘隴頽沒，永懷若人，行路慨然。

translations.literal: Later when Fan Ze was military commissioner, Haoran's tomb was low and ruined. Fu Zai sent a note to Fan Ze saying, "The late Recluse Meng Haoran, literary and substantial, outstanding and fine, fell long ago; his lineage declined, mound and ridge collapsed. Ever cherishing such a man, travelers sigh.
translations.idiomatic: Later, when Fan Ze served as military commissioner, Meng Haoran's tomb had sunk and fallen into ruin. Fu Zai wrote to Fan Ze, saying, "The late Recluse Meng Haoran was outstanding in both talent and character. He has been gone many years, his descendants have declined, and his grave mound has crumbled. All who cherish his memory, even passersby on the road, sigh at the sight.

sentences.zh: 前公欲更築大墓，闔州搢紳，聞風竦動。

translations.literal: Your Excellency formerly wished to rebuild a great tomb; the gentry of the whole prefecture were stirred at the news.
translations.idiomatic: Your Excellency once wished to rebuild a grand tomb for him, and the gentry of the entire prefecture were stirred at the news.

sentences.zh: 而今外迫軍旅，内勞賓客，牽耗歳時，或有未遑。

translations.literal: Yet now outwardly pressed by armies, inwardly wearied by guests, years drawn out in strain—perhaps there has been no leisure.
translations.idiomatic: Yet now you are pressed by military affairs from without and wearied by guests from within, and the years slip away in constant demands—perhaps there has been no time.

sentences.zh: 誠令好事者乘而有之，負公夙志矣。」

translations.literal: If indeed enthusiasts should seize the chance and take it over, that would betray Your Excellency's long-held intent."
translations.idiomatic: If enthusiasts should seize the opportunity and take the task upon themselves, that would betray the purpose Your Excellency has long cherished.

sentences.zh: 澤乃更爲刻碑鳳林山南，封寵其墓。

translations.literal: Fan Ze then had a stele carved south of Mount Fenglin and honored and enriched the tomb.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Ze then had a stele carved on the south slope of Mount Fenglin and restored and honored the tomb.

sentences.zh: 初，王維過郢州，畫浩然像于刺史亭，因曰浩然亭。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Wang Wei passed through Ying Prefecture, he painted Haoran's portrait at the prefect's pavilion, and it was therefore called the Haoran Pavilion.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when Wang Wei passed through Ying Prefecture, he painted Haoran's portrait in the prefect's pavilion, which was therefore called the Haoran Pavilion.

sentences.zh: 咸通中，刺史鄭諴謂賢者名不可斥，更署曰孟亭。

translations.literal: In the Xiantong era the prefect Zheng Yin held that a worthy man's name should not be set aside, and renamed it the Meng Pavilion.
translations.idiomatic: During the Xiantong era, Prefect Zheng Yin held that a worthy man's name should not be pushed aside, and renamed it the Meng Pavilion.

sentences.zh: 開元、天寶間，同知名者王昌齡、崔顥，皆位不顯。

translations.literal: In the Kaiyuan and Tianbao eras, Wang Changling and Cui Hao, equally renowned, both attained no conspicuous rank.
translations.idiomatic: During the Kaiyuan and Tianbao eras, Wang Changling and Cui Hao were equally famous, yet neither rose to prominent office.

sentences.zh: 附 王昌齡昌齡，字少伯，江甯人。

translations.literal: Supplement: Wang Changling—Changling, style name Shaobo, was a man of Jiangning.
translations.idiomatic: Supplement: Wang Changling, courtesy name Shaobo, was a native of Jiangning.

sentences.zh: 第進士，補秘書郎。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination and was appointed Secretary.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination and was appointed to the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 又中宏辭，遷汜水尉。

translations.literal: He also passed the hongci examination and was transferred to Assistant Magistrate of Sishui.
translations.idiomatic: He also passed the hongci literary examination and was promoted to Assistant Magistrate of Sishui.

sentences.zh: 不護細行，貶龍標尉。

translations.literal: Because he did not guard small conduct, he was demoted to Assistant Magistrate of Longbiao.
translations.idiomatic: Because he did not restrain his minor indiscretions, he was demoted to Assistant Magistrate of Longbiao.

sentences.zh: 以世亂還鄕里，爲刺史閭丘曉所殺。

translations.literal: Because of the age's disorder he returned to his home district and was killed by the prefect Luqiu Xiao.
translations.idiomatic: When the realm fell into chaos he returned home, where he was killed by the prefect Luqiu Xiao.

sentences.zh: 張鎬按軍河南，兵大集，曉最後期，將戮之，辭曰：「有親，乞貸餘命。」

translations.literal: Zhang Hao inspected the army in Henan; troops gathered in great numbers. Xiao arrived last and was about to be executed. He pleaded, "I have dependents—please spare my remaining life."
translations.idiomatic: When Zhang Hao inspected the army in Henan, the troops assembled in force. Xiao was the last to arrive and was about to be executed; he pleaded, "I have family who depend on me—please spare my life.

sentences.zh: 鎬曰：「王昌齡之親，欲與誰養？」

translations.literal: Hao said, "Wang Changling's dependents—whom do you expect to raise them?"
translations.idiomatic: Hao replied, "Wang Changling's dependents—who will support them now?"

sentences.zh: 曉默然。

translations.literal: Xiao fell silent.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao said nothing.

sentences.zh: 昌齡工詩，緒密而思淸，時謂王江寧云。

translations.literal: Changling was skilled at poetry; his texture was dense and his thought pure. People of the time called him Wang of Jiangning.
translations.idiomatic: Changling excelled at poetry; his verse was tightly woven and his thought lucid. People of the time called him "Wang of Jiangning."

sentences.zh: 附 崔顥崔顥者，亦擢進士第，有文無行。

translations.literal: Supplement: Cui Hao—Cui Hao also passed the jinshi examination; he had literary talent but no moral conduct.
translations.idiomatic: Supplement: Cui Hao also passed the jinshi examination, but though he had literary talent he lacked moral restraint.

sentences.zh: 好蒱博，嗜酒。

translations.literal: He loved gambling and was fond of wine.
translations.idiomatic: He was addicted to gambling and fond of wine.

sentences.zh: 娶妻惟擇美者，俄又棄之，凡四五娶。

translations.literal: In taking wives he selected only beautiful women, then soon abandoned them—altogether four or five marriages.
translations.idiomatic: He chose wives only for their beauty, then soon cast them aside; he married four or five times in all.

sentences.zh: 終司勳員外郎。

translations.literal: He ended as Outer Member of the Bureau of Merit.
translations.idiomatic: He ended his career as Outer Member of the Bureau of Merit.

sentences.zh: 初，李邕聞其名，虚舍邀之，顥至獻詩，首章曰：「十五嫁王昌。」

translations.literal: Earlier, when Li Yong heard his fame, he vacated his residence to invite him. Hao arrived and presented a poem whose opening line read, "At fifteen I married Wang Chang."
translations.idiomatic: When Li Yong first heard of his reputation, he cleared out his house to receive him. Hao came and presented a poem whose first line ran, "At fifteen I married Wang Chang.

sentences.zh: 邕叱曰：「小兒無禮！」

translations.literal: Yong shouted, "You impudent boy!"
translations.idiomatic: Yong shouted, "You impudent whelp!"

sentences.zh: 不與接而去。

translations.literal: He refused to receive him and sent him away.
translations.idiomatic: He refused to see him and turned him out.

sentences.zh: 劉太眞劉太眞，宣州人。

translations.literal: Liu Taizhen—Liu Taizhen was a man of Xuan Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Taizhen was a native of Xuan Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 善屬文，師蘭陵蕭穎士。

translations.literal: He was skilled at composing prose and studied under Xiao Yingshi of Lanling.
translations.idiomatic: He was skilled at literary composition and studied under Xiao Yingshi of Lanling.

sentences.zh: 舉髙第進士。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination with highest honors.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination with the highest honors.

sentences.zh: 淮南陳少遊表爲掌書記，嘗以少遊擬桓、文，爲義士所訾。

translations.literal: Chen Shaoyou of Huainan recommended him as Chief Recorder; he once likened Shaoyou to Huan and Wen and was criticized by men of integrity.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Shaoyou of Huainan recommended him as chief recorder on his staff. Taizhen once compared Shaoyou to Duke Huan of Qi and Duke Wen of Jin, and men of integrity censured him for it.

sentences.zh: 興元初，爲河東宣慰賑給使，累遷刑部侍郎。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Xingyuan era he served as Commissioner for Relief in Hedong and was repeatedly promoted to Vice Minister of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Xingyuan era he served as relief commissioner for Hedong and was promoted in stages to Vice Minister of Justice.

sentences.zh: 德宗以天下平，貞元四年九月，詔群臣宴曲江，自爲詩，敕宰相擇文人賡和。

translations.literal: Emperor Dezong, considering the realm at peace, in the ninth month of the fourth year of Zhenyuan ordered the officials to feast at Qujiang, composed a poem himself, and commanded the chief ministers to select literary men to compose matching verses.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Dezong considered the realm at peace, in the ninth month of the fourth year of Zhenyuan he ordered the court to feast at Qujiang, composed a poem himself, and commanded the chief ministers to select literary men to compose matching verses.

sentences.zh: 李泌等請群臣皆和，帝自第之，乙太眞、李紓等爲上，鮑防、于邵等次之，張濛等爲下。

translations.literal: Li Mi and others requested that all the officials compose matching poems; the emperor personally ranked them, placing Taizhen, Li Shu, and others in the top grade; Bao Fang, Yu Shao, and others in the second; Zhang Meng and others in the lowest.
translations.idiomatic: Li Mi and others asked that all the officials compose matching poems. The emperor personally ranked them, placing Taizhen, Li Shu, and others in the top tier; Bao Fang, Yu Shao, and others in the second; and Zhang Meng and others in the lowest.

sentences.zh: 與擇者四十一人，惟泌、李晟、馬燧三宰相無所差次。

translations.literal: Among the forty-one selected for ranking, only the three chief ministers Mi, Li Sheng, and Ma Sui received no separate grade.
translations.idiomatic: Of the forty-one men chosen for ranking, only the three chief ministers Mi, Li Sheng, and Ma Sui were given no separate grade.

sentences.zh: 遷禮部，掌貢士，多取大臣貴近子弟，坐貶信州刺史，卒。

translations.literal: He was transferred to the Ministry of Rites and oversaw the examination of candidates; he took too many sons and relatives of great ministers and the imperial kin, and for this was demoted to Prefect of Xin Prefecture, where he died.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to the Ministry of Rites to oversee the civil examinations, but admitted too many sons and relatives of high ministers and the imperial kin. For this he was demoted to Prefect of Xin Prefecture, where he died.

sentences.zh: 邵説邵説，相州安陽人。

translations.literal: Shao Shuo—Shuo was a man of Anyang in Xiang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Shao Shuo was a native of Anyang in Xiang Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 已擢進士第，未調，陷史思明。

translations.literal: Having already passed the jinshi examination, before he received appointment he fell into the hands of Shi Siming.
translations.idiomatic: He had already passed the jinshi examination but had not yet received an appointment when he fell into the hands of Shi Siming.

sentences.zh: 逮朝義敗，歸郭子儀，子儀愛其才，留幕府。

translations.literal: When Chaoyi was defeated, he went to Guo Ziyi; Ziyi admired his talent and kept him on his staff.
translations.idiomatic: When Shi Chaoyi was defeated, he went over to Guo Ziyi, who admired his talent and kept him on his staff.

sentences.zh: 遷累長安令、秘書少監。

translations.literal: Through successive promotions he rose to Magistrate of Chang'an and Deputy Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Through successive promotions he rose to Magistrate of Chang'an and Deputy Director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 大暦末，上言：「天道三十年一小變，六十年一大變。

translations.literal: At the end of the Dali era he submitted a memorial: "Heaven's Way shifts in small cycles every thirty years and in great cycles every sixty years.
translations.idiomatic: Near the end of the Dali era he submitted a memorial: "Heaven's Way undergoes a small transformation every thirty years and a great transformation every sixty years.

sentences.zh: 祿山、思明之難，出入二紀，多難漸平，向之亂，今將變而之治。

translations.literal: The calamities of Lushan and Siming have spanned nearly two twelve-year cycles; as many tribulations gradually subside, what was disorder is now about to turn toward order.
translations.idiomatic: The disasters of An Lushan and Shi Siming have spanned nearly two twelve-year cycles. As the many calamities gradually subside, the age of disorder is now turning toward order.

sentences.zh: 宜建徽號，承天意。

translations.literal: An auspicious reign title should be established to accord with Heaven's intent.
translations.idiomatic: An auspicious reign title should be established to accord with Heaven's will.

sentences.zh: 而方謁郊廟、大赦各一，誠恐雲雨之施未普，鬱結之氣未除。

translations.literal: Yet we have had only one visit to the suburban altars and one general amnesty; truly one fears the rain of grace has not been widely bestowed and the air of pent-up resentment has not been cleared.
translations.idiomatic: Yet there has been only one visit to the suburban altars and one general amnesty. I truly fear that Heaven's rain of grace has not been widely bestowed and the air of pent-up resentment has not yet been dispelled.

sentences.zh: 願因此時修享獻、款郊廟、褒有德、録賢人，與天下更始，振災益壽之術也。」

translations.literal: I wish that at this time sacrificial offerings be properly performed, the suburban altars be reverently approached, the virtuous be praised, and worthy men be recorded—to renew the realm with the people and revive the art of dispelling calamity and prolonging life."
translations.idiomatic: I ask that at this time proper sacrifices be performed, the suburban altars be reverently approached, the virtuous be honored, and worthy men be recorded, so that the realm may begin anew with the people and the means of dispelling disaster and prolonging life may be restored.

sentences.zh: 不聽。

translations.literal: [The emperor] did not approve.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor did not heed the proposal.

sentences.zh: 德宗立，擢吏部侍郎。

translations.literal: When Emperor Dezong ascended the throne, [Shuo] was promoted to Vice Minister of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Dezong ascended the throne, Shuo was promoted to Vice Minister of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 説因自陳：「家本儒，先祖長白山人貞一，以武后革命，終身不肯仕。

translations.literal: Shuo therefore presented his own account: "My family was originally Confucian. My ancestor Zhenyī of Changbai Mountain, because of Empress Wu's usurpation, refused office for his entire life.
translations.idiomatic: Shuo therefore presented his own account: "My family was originally Confucian. My ancestor Zhenyī of Changbai Mountain, because of Empress Wu's usurpation, refused to serve for his entire life.

sentences.zh: 先臣殿中侍御史瓊之，逮事玄宗。

translations.literal: My late father Qiongzhī, Palace Attendant Censor, served Emperor Xuanzong.
translations.idiomatic: My late father Qiongzhī, a Palace Attendant Censor, served Emperor Xuanzong.

sentences.zh: 臣十六即孤，長育母手，天寶中始仕。

translations.literal: I was orphaned at sixteen and was raised by my mother's hand; I first entered office in the Tianbao era.
translations.idiomatic: I was orphaned at sixteen and was raised by my mother; I first entered office during the Tianbao era.

sentences.zh: 會喪，客河北，祿山亂，喪紀當終，臣不褫衰絰又再期，懼終不免，陰走洺、魏。

translations.literal: When I was in mourning, I was staying in Hebei; Lushan's rebellion broke out. My mourning period should have ended, yet I did not lay aside my mourning garments for another full cycle, fearing I could not escape in the end, and secretly fled toward Ming and Wei.
translations.idiomatic: While I was in mourning and staying in Hebei, Lushan's rebellion broke out. My mourning period should have ended, yet I did not lay aside my mourning garments for another full cycle, fearing I could not escape, and secretly fled toward Ming and Wei.

sentences.zh: 慶緒遁保西城，搜脅儒者爲己用，以兵迫臣，遂陷醜逆。

translations.literal: Qingxu fled to hold Xicheng, searched out and coerced scholars for his use, pressed me with troops, and so I fell among the foul rebels.
translations.idiomatic: When Shi Qingxu fled to hold Xicheng, he searched out and coerced scholars into his service, pressed me with troops, and so I fell among the foul rebels.

sentences.zh: 俄而史思明順附，欲間道歸北闕下，肅宗拜臣左金吾衞騎曹參軍，許留思明所。

translations.literal: Soon afterward Shi Siming submitted to the court; wishing to return by a secret route to the northern capital, I was appointed by Emperor Suzong as Cavalry Commandant in the Left Jinwu Guard, with permission to remain in Siming's territory.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward Shi Siming submitted to the court. Wishing to return by a secret route to the northern capital, I was appointed by Emperor Suzong as Cavalry Commandant in the Left Jinwu Guard, with permission to remain in Siming's territory.

sentences.zh: 會烏承恩事，路絶，不得歸。

translations.literal: When the Wu Chengen affair occurred, the route was cut off and I could not return.
translations.idiomatic: When the Wu Chengen affair occurred, the route was cut off and I could not return.

sentences.zh: 朝義之敗，欲固守河陽，臣知回紇利野戰，陰勸其行，以破賊計。

translations.literal: When Chaoyi was defeated and wished to hold firm at Heyang, knowing the Uyghurs were adept at field battle, I secretly urged them to march out, so as to break the rebels' plan.
translations.idiomatic: When Chaoyi was defeated and wished to hold firm at Heyang, knowing the Uyghurs excelled at field battle, I secretly urged them to march out and thereby break the rebels' plan.

sentences.zh: 朝義已走，臣西歸獻狀，先帝詔翰林索臣所上言，與王伷偕召。

translations.literal: After Chaoyi had fled, I returned west and submitted my account; the late emperor ordered the Hanlin Academy to retrieve my memorials and summoned me together with Wang Zhou.
translations.idiomatic: After Chaoyi had fled, I returned west and submitted my account. The late emperor ordered the Hanlin Academy to retrieve my memorials and summoned me together with Wang Zhou.

sentences.zh: 先帝謂誠節白著，故擢伷侍御史，臣爲殿中侍御史，使者宣旨制詔盡言其狀，則疇昔本末，先帝知之。

translations.literal: The late emperor considered our loyalty evident and therefore promoted Zhou to Attendant Censor and me to Palace Attendant Censor; the envoy proclaimed the edict and imperial decree fully stating our circumstances—so from first to last the late emperor knew [my story].
translations.idiomatic: The late emperor considered our loyalty evident and therefore promoted Zhou to Attendant Censor and me to Palace Attendant Censor. The envoy proclaimed the edict and imperial decree fully stating our circumstances, so from first to last the late emperor knew my story.

sentences.zh: 今又擢以不次，雖自天斷，尚恐受謗輿人，傷陛下之明。

translations.literal: Now I am again promoted out of turn; though the decision comes from Heaven, I still fear slander from the common crowd and injury to Your Majesty's clear judgment.
translations.idiomatic: Now I am again promoted out of turn. Though the decision comes from Heaven, I still fear slander from the common people and injury to Your Majesty's clear judgment.

sentences.zh: 今吏員未乏而調者多，益以功優，准平格以判留，人去者十七，彼且鼓讒説以投疑於上，此臣所大懼也。」

translations.literal: Now the bureaus are not short of personnel yet many await assignment; adding merit promotion and allowing retention by ordinary grade, seventeen men will be passed over—they will surely stir up slander to cast suspicion on Your Majesty. This is what I greatly fear."
translations.idiomatic: The bureaus are not short of personnel, yet many await assignment. Adding merit promotion and allowing retention by ordinary grade, seventeen men will be passed over—they will surely stir up slander to cast suspicion on Your Majesty. This is what I greatly fear.

sentences.zh: 因薦戸部郎中蕭定、司農卿庾准自代，不許。

translations.literal: He therefore recommended Bureau Director Xiao Ding and Minister of Revenue Yu Zhun as his replacements, but was not permitted.
translations.idiomatic: He therefore recommended Bureau Director Xiao Ding and Minister of Revenue Yu Zhun to replace him, but the request was denied.

sentences.zh: 説在職以才顯，或言且執政，金吾將軍裴儆謂柳載曰：「説事賊爲劇官，掌其兵，大小百戰，掠名家子爲奴婢不可計，得宥死而無厚顏，乃崇第産，附貴幸。

translations.literal: While in office Shuo's talent made him conspicuous, and some said he would soon enter the government. General of the Jinwu Guard Pei Jun said to Liu Zai: "Shuo served the rebels in a major post, commanded their troops, fought a hundred battles great and small, and carried off sons of noble families as slaves and maidservants beyond reckoning. Having been spared death, he shows no shame—instead he builds grand mansions and attaches himself to the powerful and favored.
translations.idiomatic: While in office Shuo's talent made him conspicuous, and some said he would soon hold power. General of the Jinwu Guard Pei Jun said to Liu Zai: "Shuo served the rebels in a major post, commanded their troops, fought a hundred battles great and small, and carried off sons of noble families as slaves and maidservants beyond reckoning. Having been spared death, he shows no shame—instead he builds grand mansions and attaches himself to the powerful and favored.

sentences.zh: 欲以相邦，其能久乎！」

translations.literal: And now they would make him chief minister—can he last long?"
translations.idiomatic: And now they would make him chief minister—can he last long?

sentences.zh: 建中三年逐嚴郢，説與郢善，微諷硃泚訟其冤，爲草奏，貶歸州刺史，卒。

translations.literal: In the third year of Jianzhong, when Yan Ying was driven out, Shuo was on good terms with Ying and subtly prompted Zhu Ci to plead his injustice; he drafted the memorial, was demoted to Prefect of Gui Prefecture, and died.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Jianzhong, when Yan Ying was driven out, Shuo was on good terms with Ying and subtly prompted Zhu Ci to plead his injustice. He drafted the memorial, was demoted to Prefect of Gui Prefecture, and died.

sentences.zh: 于邵于邵字相門，其先自代來，爲京兆萬年人。

translations.literal: Yu Shao—Shao, style name Xiangmen, his ancestors having come from Dai, were natives of Wannian in Jingzhao.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Shao, courtesy name Xiangmen, was descended from a family that had come from Dai and was registered as a native of Wannian in Jingzhao.

sentences.zh: 天寶末，第進士，以書判超絶，補崇文校書郎。

translations.literal: At the end of the Tianbao era he passed the jinshi examination; for his outstanding performance in the document-judgment test he was appointed Proofreader in the Chongwen Institute.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Tianbao era he passed the jinshi examination. For his outstanding performance in the document-judgment test he was appointed Proofreader in the Chongwen Institute.

sentences.zh: 繇比部郎中爲道州刺史，未行，徙巴州。

translations.literal: From Bureau Director in the Ministry of Revenue he was made Prefect of Dao Prefecture; before he took up the post he was transferred to Ba Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: From Bureau Director in the Ministry of Revenue he was appointed Prefect of Dao Prefecture, but before he took up the post he was transferred to Ba Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 會歳饑，部獠亂，薄城下。

translations.literal: There happened to be famine; the tribal people of the department rebelled and pressed close under the city walls.
translations.idiomatic: There happened to be famine, and the tribal people of the prefecture rebelled and pressed close under the city walls.

sentences.zh: 邵勵兵拒戰，且遣使諭曉，獠丐降，邵儒服出，賊見皆拜，即引去。

translations.literal: Shao encouraged his troops to resist and also sent envoys to persuade and enlighten them; the tribesmen begged to surrender. Shao went out in Confucian robes; when the rebels saw him they all bowed, and withdrew at once.
translations.idiomatic: Shao encouraged his troops to resist and also sent envoys to persuade them. The tribesmen begged to surrender. Shao went out in Confucian robes; when the rebels saw him they all bowed and withdrew at once.

sentences.zh: 節度使李抱玉以聞，遷梓州，辭疾不拜，授兵部郎中。

translations.literal: The military commissioner Li Baoyu reported this; [Shao] was transferred to Zizhou but declined the appointment on grounds of illness and was given the post of Bureau Director in the Ministry of War.
translations.idiomatic: The military commissioner Li Baoyu reported this. Shao was transferred to Zizhou but declined the appointment on grounds of illness and was given the post of Bureau Director in the Ministry of War.

sentences.zh: 崔寧帥蜀，表爲度支副使。

translations.literal: When Cui Ning commanded Shu, [Shao] was recommended as Deputy Commissioner of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: When Cui Ning commanded Shu, Shao was recommended as Deputy Commissioner of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 俄以諫議大夫知制誥，進禮部侍郎，朝有大典冊，必出其手。

translations.literal: Soon he served as Drafting Officer with the title Remonstrance Counselor, advanced to Vice Minister of Rites; whenever the court had great ceremonies or edicts, they invariably came from his hand.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he served as Drafting Officer with the title Remonstrance Counselor and was promoted to Vice Minister of Rites. Whenever the court had great ceremonies or edicts, they invariably came from his hand.

sentences.zh: 爲三司使，治薛邕獄，失德宗旨，貶桂州長史。

translations.literal: Serving as Commissioner of the Three Offices, he investigated the case of Xue Yong and failed to grasp the emperor's intent; he was demoted to Chief Administrator of Gui Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Serving as Commissioner of the Three Offices, he investigated the case of Xue Yong and failed to grasp the emperor's intent. He was demoted to Chief Administrator of Gui Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 復爲太子賓客，與宰相陸贄不平，出杭州刺史。

translations.literal: He was again made Advisor to the Crown Prince; he was on bad terms with Chief Minister Lu Zan and was sent out as Prefect of Hang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He was again made Advisor to the Crown Prince, but was on bad terms with Chief Minister Lu Zan and was sent out as Prefect of Hang Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 久疾求告，貶衢州別駕，徙江州。

translations.literal: After long illness he requested leave and was demoted to Vice Prefect of Qu Prefecture, then transferred to Jiang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: After a long illness he requested leave and was demoted to Vice Prefect of Qu Prefecture, then transferred to Jiang Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 卒，年八十一。

translations.literal: He died at the age of eighty-one.
translations.idiomatic: He died at the age of eighty-one.

sentences.zh: 邵孝悌有行，晩塗益修絜。

translations.literal: Shao was filial, respectful, and of upright conduct; in his later years he became still more strict in self-cultivation.
translations.idiomatic: Shao was filial, respectful, and upright in conduct; in his later years he became still more strict in self-cultivation.

sentences.zh: 樊澤始舉賢良，邵望見，曰：「將相材也。」

translations.literal: When Fan Ze first submitted to the xiangliang examination, Shao saw him from afar and said, "Material for minister and general."
translations.idiomatic: When Fan Ze first submitted to the xiangliang examination, Shao saw him from afar and said, "Here is material for a minister or general.

sentences.zh: 崔元翰舉進士，年五十矣，邵以其文擢異等，曰：「後當司詔令。」

translations.literal: When Cui Yuanhan took the jinshi examination at the age of fifty, Shao ranked his essays in the highest class and said, "Later he will draft imperial edicts."
translations.idiomatic: When Cui Yuanhan took the jinshi examination at the age of fifty, Shao ranked his essays in the highest class and said, "Later he will draft imperial edicts."

sentences.zh: 已而皆然。

translations.literal: In time both proved true.
translations.idiomatic: In time both proved true.

sentences.zh: 獨孤授舉博學宏辭，吏部考當乙，邵覆之，置甲科，人咨其公。

translations.literal: When Dugu Shou submitted to the boxue hongci examination, the Ministry of Personnel graded him second class; Shao reviewed it and placed him in first class—the people praised his fairness.
translations.idiomatic: When Dugu Shou submitted to the boxue hongci examination, the Ministry of Personnel graded him second class. Shao reviewed the result and placed him in first class, and people praised his fairness.

sentences.zh: 崔元翰崔元翰名鵬，以字行。

translations.literal: Cui Yuanhan—Yuanhan's given name was Peng; he went by his courtesy name.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Yuanhan's given name was Peng; he went by his courtesy name.

sentences.zh: 父良佐，與齊國公日用從昆弟也。

translations.literal: His father Liangzuo was a cousin of the Duke of Qi, Riyong.
translations.idiomatic: His father Liangzuo was a cousin of the Duke of Qi, Riyong.

sentences.zh: 擢明經甲科，補湖城主簿，以母喪，遂不仕。

translations.literal: He passed the mingjing examination in first class and was appointed Chief Clerk of Hucheng; upon his mother's death he ceased holding office.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the mingjing examination in first class and was appointed Chief Clerk of Hucheng, but upon his mother's death he ceased holding office.

sentences.zh: 治詩、易、書、春秋，譔演範、忘象、渾天等論數十篇。

translations.literal: He studied the Odes, Changes, Documents, and Spring and Autumn Annals, and composed dozens of treatises such as "Expounding the Model," "Forgetting Images," and "On the Armillary Sphere."
translations.idiomatic: He studied the Odes, Changes, Documents, and Spring and Autumn Annals, and composed dozens of treatises such as "Expounding the Model," "Forgetting Images," and "On the Armillary Sphere."

sentences.zh: 隱共北白鹿山之陽。

translations.literal: He lived in seclusion on the southern slope of White Deer Mountain at Gongbei.
translations.idiomatic: He lived in seclusion on the southern slope of White Deer Mountain at Gongbei.

sentences.zh: 卒，門人共謚曰貞文孝父。

translations.literal: He died; his disciples jointly gave him the posthumous title "Loyal, Literary, Filial Father."
translations.idiomatic: When he died, his disciples jointly gave him the posthumous title "Loyal, Literary, Filial Father."

sentences.zh: 元翰舉進士、博學宏辭、賢良方正，皆異等。

translations.literal: Yuanhan passed the jinshi, boxue hongci, and xiangliang examinations—all in the highest class.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanhan passed the jinshi, boxue hongci, and xiangliang examinations—all in the highest class.

sentences.zh: 義成李勉表在幕府，馬燧更表爲太原掌書記。

translations.literal: Li Mian of Yicheng recommended him for his staff; Ma Sui again recommended him as Chief Recorder at Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Li Mian of Yicheng recommended him for his staff, and Ma Sui again recommended him as chief recorder at Taiyuan.

sentences.zh: 召拜禮部員外郎。

translations.literal: He was summoned and appointed Outer Member of the Ministry of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: He was summoned and appointed Outer Member of the Ministry of Rites.

sentences.zh: 竇參秉政，引知制誥。

translations.literal: When Dou Can held power, [Can] brought him in as Drafting Officer.
translations.idiomatic: When Dou Can held power, he brought Yuanhan in as Drafting Officer.

sentences.zh: 其訓辭温厚，有典誥風。

translations.literal: His directive prose was warm and generous, with the tone of classical edicts.
translations.idiomatic: His directive prose was warm and generous, with the tone of classical edicts.

sentences.zh: 然性剛褊，不能取容於時，孤特自恃。

translations.literal: Yet his nature was stern and narrow; he could not yield to win favor in his time and relied on his solitary integrity.
translations.idiomatic: Yet his nature was stern and narrow; he could not yield to win favor in his time and relied on his solitary integrity.

sentences.zh: 掌誥凡再期，不遷，罷爲比部郎中，時已七十餘，卒。

translations.literal: He held the drafting post for two full terms without promotion, was dismissed to Bureau Director in the Ministry of Revenue, was already over seventy, and died.
translations.idiomatic: He held the drafting post for two full terms without promotion, was dismissed to Bureau Director in the Ministry of Revenue, was already over seventy, and died.

sentences.zh: 其好學老不倦，用思精緻，馳騁班固、蔡邕間以自名家。

translations.literal: He loved learning and never tired of it in old age; his application of thought was refined and meticulous, and he ranged between Ban Gu and Cai Yong to make a name for himself.
translations.idiomatic: He loved learning and never tired of it in old age. His thought was refined and meticulous, and he ranged between Ban Gu and Cai Yong to make a name for himself.

sentences.zh: 怨陸贄、李充，乃附裴延齡，延齡表鉤校京兆妄費，持吏甚急，而充等自無過，訖不能傅致以罪云。

translations.literal: Harbouring resentment against Lu Zan and Li Chong, he attached himself to Pei Yanling; Yanling memorialized to audit wasteful spending in the capital and pressed officials very harshly, yet Chong and the others had no fault—in the end no crime could be attached to them.
translations.idiomatic: Harbouring resentment against Lu Zan and Li Chong, he attached himself to Pei Yanling. Yanling memorialized to audit wasteful spending in the capital and pressed officials very harshly, yet Chong and the others were without fault—in the end no crime could be attached to them.

sentences.zh: 于公異于公異，蘇州呉人。

translations.literal: Yu Gongyi—Gongyi was a man of Wu in Suzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Gongyi was a native of Wu in Suzhou.

sentences.zh: 進士擢第，李晟表爲招討府掌書記。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination; Li Sheng recommended him as Chief Recorder on the Pacification Staff.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination, and Li Sheng recommended him as chief recorder on the Pacification Staff.

sentences.zh: 朱泚平，露布於德宗曰：「臣既肅淸宮禁，祗奉寢園，鍾𥲤不移，廟貌如故。」

translations.literal: When Zhu Ci was pacified, [Li Sheng's] victory bulletin to Emperor Dezong read: "Your subject has already cleared and purified the palace precincts and reverently tended the imperial tombs; bells and drums remain unmoved, and the temple halls are as before."
translations.idiomatic: When Zhu Ci was pacified, the victory bulletin to Emperor Dezong read: "Your subject has already cleared and purified the palace precincts and reverently tended the imperial tombs; bells and drums remain unmoved, and the temple halls are as before.

sentences.zh: 帝覽泣下，曰：「誰爲之辭？」

translations.literal: When the emperor read it, he wept and said, "Who wrote these words?"
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor read it, he wept and said, "Who wrote these words?"

sentences.zh: 或以公異對，帝咨歎一再。

translations.literal: Some answered that it was Gongyi; the emperor sighed in admiration again and again.
translations.idiomatic: Some answered that it was Gongyi, and the emperor sighed in admiration again and again.

sentences.zh: 始，公異與陸贄故有隙，時贄在翰林，聞不喜。

translations.literal: From the first Gongyi and Lu Zan had an old rift; at the time Zan was in the Hanlin Academy and, on hearing this, was displeased.
translations.idiomatic: From the first Gongyi and Lu Zan had an old rift. At the time Zan was in the Hanlin Academy, and on hearing this he was displeased.

sentences.zh: 世多言公異不能事後母，既仕不歸省。

translations.literal: Many in the world said Gongyi could not serve his stepmother properly and, once in office, did not return home to visit his family.
translations.idiomatic: Many said that Gongyi failed to treat his stepmother properly and, once in office, did not return home to visit his family.

sentences.zh: 及贄當政，乃奏其狀，詔賜孝經，罷歸田里。

translations.literal: When Zan came to power, he memorialized about his conduct; an edict bestowed the Classic of Filial Piety upon him and dismissed him to return to his home district.
translations.idiomatic: When Zan came to power, he memorialized about his conduct. An edict bestowed the Classic of Filial Piety upon him and dismissed him to return home.

sentences.zh: 盧邁坐舉非其人，奪俸兩月。

translations.literal: Lu Mai was punished for recommending an unworthy man and had his salary withheld for two months.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Mai was punished for recommending an unworthy man and had his salary withheld for two months.

sentences.zh: 時中書舍人髙郢，嘗薦御史元敦義，及公異被譴，郢亦劾敦義無美行，詔免敦義官。

translations.literal: At the time the Drafting Officer Gao Ying had once recommended Attendant Censor Yuan Dunyi; when Gongyi was censured, Ying also impeached Dunyi for lacking fine conduct, and an edict removed Dunyi from office.
translations.idiomatic: At the time the Drafting Officer Gao Ying had once recommended Attendant Censor Yuan Dunyi. When Gongyi was censured, Ying also impeached Dunyi for lacking fine conduct, and an edict removed Dunyi from office.

sentences.zh: 公異繇是不自振而卒。

translations.literal: Gongyi therefore never recovered himself and died.
translations.idiomatic: Gongyi therefore never recovered his standing and died.

sentences.zh: 李益李益，故宰相揆族子，於詩尤所長。

translations.literal: Li Yi—Yi was a clansman of the former chief minister Kui and was especially skilled in poetry.
translations.idiomatic: Li Yi was a clansman of the former chief minister Li Kui and was especially skilled in poetry.

sentences.zh: 貞元末，名與宗人賀相埒。

translations.literal: At the end of Zhenyuan his fame was on a par with his clansman He.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Zhenyuan era his fame was on a par with that of his clansman He.

sentences.zh: 毎一篇成，樂工爭以賂求取之，被聲歌，供奉天子。

translations.literal: Whenever a poem was finished, musicians competed to bribe him for copies; set to music, they were performed for the Son of Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever he finished a poem, musicians competed to bribe him for copies. Set to music, his poems were performed for the emperor.

sentences.zh: 至征人、早行等篇，天下皆施之圖繪。

translations.literal: As for such pieces as "Conscript" and "Early Departure," all were illustrated throughout the realm.
translations.idiomatic: Such pieces as "Conscript" and "Early Departure" were illustrated throughout the realm.

sentences.zh: 少癡而忌克，防閑妻妾苛嚴，世謂妬爲「李益疾」。

translations.literal: From youth foolish yet jealous and envious, guarding and restraining wives and concubines with harsh severity; the age called jealousy "Li Yi's ailment."
translations.idiomatic: Even as a young man he was both simple-minded and fiercely jealous; he kept such harsh watch over his wives and concubines that people of the day nicknamed jealousy "Li Yi's disease."

sentences.zh: 同輩行稍稍進顯，益獨不調，鬱鬱去。

translations.literal: Peers of his generation gradually advanced to prominence; Yi alone received no appointment, and left in dejection.
translations.idiomatic: His contemporaries gradually rose to prominence one after another, but Yi alone failed to secure an appointment and departed in gloomy frustration.

sentences.zh: 游燕，劉濟辟置幕府，進爲營田副使。

translations.literal: Travelling in Yan, Liu Ji recruited and placed him in the military staff; he advanced to become Deputy Commissioner of garrison fields.
translations.idiomatic: While traveling in Yan territory, Liu Ji recruited him to his staff; he was promoted to Deputy Commissioner of Garrison Fields.

sentences.zh: 嘗與濟詩，語怨望。

translations.literal: Once when exchanging poems with Ji, his language expressed resentment and discontent.
translations.idiomatic: On one occasion, in poems exchanged with Liu Ji, he expressed bitter resentment.

sentences.zh: 憲宗雅知名，召爲祕書少監、集不能堪，諫官因暴幽州時怨望語，詔降秩。

translations.literal: Emperor Xianzong had long known his reputation, summoned him as Vice Director of the Secretariat; Ji could not bear it; remonstrating officials thereupon exposed his resentful words from Youzhou days, and an edict demoted his rank.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xianzong, who had long admired his literary renown, summoned Li Yi to serve as Vice Director of the Secretariat, but Yi could not endure the post. Remonstrating officials then made public the resentful language he had used while at Youzhou, and an edict lowered his rank.

sentences.zh: 俄復舊官，累遷集賢殿學士。

translations.literal: Before long his former office was restored; he was repeatedly promoted to Academician of the Hall of Assembled Worthies.
translations.idiomatic: Shortly afterward his former rank was restored, and he rose through successive appointments to Academician of the Hall of Assembled Worthies.

sentences.zh: 自負才，凌藉士，右散騎常侍。

translations.literal: Confident in his talent, he trampled upon and insulted scholars; [he reached the post of] Right Regular Companion.
translations.idiomatic: Conceited about his gifts, he looked down on and humiliated other scholars; he eventually served as Right Regular Companion.

sentences.zh: 大和初，以禮部尚書致仕，卒。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Dahe reign, he retired as Minister of Rites and died.
translations.idiomatic: In the early Dahe era he retired from office as Minister of Rites and died.

sentences.zh: 時又有太子庶子李益同在朝，故世言「文章李益」以辨云。

translations.literal: At that time there was also a Li Yi serving as Vice Director of the Crown Prince's Household in court together with him; hence the age spoke of "Li Yi the man of letters" to distinguish them, it is said.
translations.idiomatic: At the same time another Li Yi, Vice Director of the Crown Prince's Household, was also at court; and so people of the day distinguished them by calling the poet "Li Yi the literary man."

sentences.zh: 盧綸盧綸字允言，河中蒲人。

translations.literal: Lu Lun — Lu Lun, styled Yunyan, a native of Pu in Hezhong.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Lun, courtesy name Yunyan, was a native of Pu in Hezhong circuit.

sentences.zh: 避天寶亂，客鄱陽。

translations.literal: Fleeing the Tianbao turmoil, he sojourned as a guest at Poyang.
translations.idiomatic: During the Tianbao rebellion he fled south and lived as a guest in Poyang.

sentences.zh: 大暦初，數舉進士不入第。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Dali reign, he repeatedly entered the jinshi examination but did not pass.
translations.idiomatic: In the early Dali era he sat for the jinshi examination several times but never passed.

sentences.zh: 元載取綸文以進，補閿鄕尉。

translations.literal: Yuan Zai selected Lun's writings and presented them; [Lun] was appointed Assistant Magistrate of Wen Township.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Zai forwarded samples of Lun's writing to the throne, and Lun was appointed Assistant Magistrate of Wen Township.

sentences.zh: 累遷監察御史，輒稱疾去。

translations.literal: Through repeated promotions he reached Censor; he then claimed illness and departed.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through successive posts to Censor, but soon claimed illness and resigned.

sentences.zh: 坐與王縉善，久不調。

translations.literal: Because of being close to Wang Jin, for a long time he received no appointment.
translations.idiomatic: Because of his friendship with Wang Jin, he went for a long stretch without receiving any appointment.

sentences.zh: 渾瑊鎭河中，辟元帥判官，累遷檢校戸部郎中。

translations.literal: Hun Jian garrisoned Hezhong; [Lun] was recruited as military staff judge; through repeated promotions he became Acting Director in the Ministry of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: When Hun Jian commanded Hezhong, Lun joined his staff as a military judge and was promoted over time to Acting Director in the Ministry of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 嘗朝京師，是時，舅韋渠牟得幸德宗，表其才，召見禁中，帝有所作，輒使賡和。

translations.literal: Once he came to court at the capital; at that time his maternal uncle Wei Qumou enjoyed Emperor Dezong's favor, memorialized his talent, and he was summoned to an audience within the palace; whenever the Emperor composed something, he was always ordered to continue and harmonize with it.
translations.idiomatic: On one visit to the capital, his maternal uncle Wei Qumou, who then enjoyed Emperor Dezong's favor, recommended his talent to the throne. Summoned to an audience within the palace, Lun was whenever the emperor composed a poem, always assigned to compose a matching verse.

sentences.zh: 異日問渠牟：「盧綸、李益何在？」

translations.literal: On another day [the Emperor] asked Qumou: "Where are Lu Lun and Li Yi?
translations.idiomatic: Another day the emperor asked Wei Qumou, "Where are Lu Lun and Li Yi?

sentences.zh: 答曰：「綸從渾瑊在河中。」

translations.literal: He answered: "Lun follows Hun Jian in Hezhong."
translations.idiomatic: He replied, "Lun is with Hun Jian in Hezhong."

sentences.zh: 驛召之，會卒。

translations.literal: An urgent dispatch summoned him; just then [Lun] died.
translations.idiomatic: A courier was sent to summon him at once, but Lun died before he could arrive.

sentences.zh: 綸與吉中孚、韓翃、錢起、司空曙、苗發、崔峒、耿湋、夏侯審、李端皆能詩齊名，號「大暦十才子」。

translations.literal: Lun together with Ji Zhongfu, Han Hong, Qian Qi, Sikong Shu, Miao Fa, Cui Tong, Geng Wei, Xiahou Shen, and Li Duan were all alike famed for poetry, and were styled "the Ten Talented Men of Dali."
translations.idiomatic: Lun, together with Ji Zhongfu, Han Hong, Qian Qi, Sikong Shu, Miao Fa, Cui Tong, Geng Wei, Xiahou Shen, and Li Duan, all won equal renown for poetry and were known as "the Ten Talented Literati of the Dali Era."

sentences.zh: 憲宗詔中書舍人張仲素訪集遺文。

translations.literal: Emperor Xianzong ordered Palace Draftsman Zhang Zhongsu to seek and gather his surviving writings.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xianzong ordered the Palace Draftsman Zhang Zhongsu to collect his surviving writings.

sentences.zh: 文宗尤愛其詩，問宰相：「綸文章幾何？

translations.literal: Emperor Wenzong especially loved his poems, and asked the chief ministers: "How many writings of Lun are there?
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wenzong was especially fond of his poetry and asked the chief ministers, "How many of Lun's literary works survive?

sentences.zh: 亦有子否？」

translations.literal: Does he also have sons?
translations.idiomatic: Did he also leave sons?

sentences.zh: 李德裕對：「綸四子：簡能、簡辭、弘止、簡求，皆擢進士第，在臺閣。」

translations.literal: Li Deyu replied: "Lun had four sons: Jianneng, Jianci, Hongzhi, and Jianqiu; all passed the jinshi examination and serve in the central administration."
