translations.idiomatic: Li Deyu answered, "Lun had four sons—Jianneng, Jianci, Hongzhi, and Jianqiu—all of whom passed the jinshi examination and serve in the central administration."

sentences.zh: 帝遣中人悉索家笥，得詩五百篇以聞。

translations.literal: The Emperor sent eunuchs to search through all the family chests, obtained five hundred poems and had them reported.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent palace eunuchs to search the family chests thoroughly; five hundred poems were found and presented to the throne.

sentences.zh: 附 吉中孚中孚，鄱陽人。

translations.literal: Appended — Ji Zhongfu: Zhongfu, a native of Poyang.
translations.idiomatic: Appended biography: Ji Zhongfu, a native of Poyang.

sentences.zh: 官戸部侍郎。

translations.literal: His office was Vice Minister of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: He served as Vice Minister of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 附 韓翃翃字君平，南陽人。

translations.literal: Appended — Han Hong: Hong, styled Junping, a native of Nanyang.
translations.idiomatic: Appended biography: Han Hong, courtesy name Junping, a native of Nanyang.

sentences.zh: 侯希逸表佐淄靑幕府，府罷，十年不出。

translations.literal: Hou Xiyi memorialized [recommending] him as staff assistant in the Ziqing military governorship; when that headquarters was abolished, for ten years he did not go out [into office].
translations.idiomatic: Hou Xiyi recommended him for a post on the Ziqing military staff; when that headquarters was disbanded, Han did not take office again for ten years.

sentences.zh: 李勉在宣武，復辟之。

translations.literal: When Li Mian was at Xuanyi Wu, he again recruited him.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Mian took command at Xuanyu Wu, he recruited Han again.

sentences.zh: 俄以駕部郎中知制誥。

translations.literal: Before long, as Director in the Department of Carriages, he was assigned to draft edicts.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he was appointed Director in the Department of Carriages and entrusted with drafting imperial edicts.

sentences.zh: 時有兩韓翃，其一爲刺史，宰相請孰與，德宗曰：「與詩人韓翃。」

translations.literal: At that time there were two Han Hongs; one was a prefect; the chief ministers asked which should receive [the appointment], and Dezong said: "Give it to Han Hong the poet.
translations.idiomatic: At the time two men named Han Hong were in government service, one of them a prefect; when the chief ministers asked which man should receive the appointment, Emperor Dezong said, "Give it to Han Hong the poet.

sentences.zh: 終中書舍人。

translations.literal: He ended as Palace Draftsman.
translations.idiomatic: He eventually rose to Palace Draftsman.

sentences.zh: 附 錢起起，呉興人。

translations.literal: Appended — Qian Qi: Qi, a native of Wuxing.
translations.idiomatic: Appended biography: Qian Qi, a native of Wuxing.

sentences.zh: 天寶中舉進士，與郎士元齊名，時語曰：「前有沈、宋，後有錢、郎。」

translations.literal: In the Tianbao era he passed the jinshi examination; he was equally famed with Lang Shiyuan; a saying of the time ran: "Before there were Shen and Song; after there are Qian and Lang.
translations.idiomatic: During the Tianbao era he passed the jinshi examination and shared equal renown with Lang Shiyuan; people of the day said, "Before there were Shen and Song; afterward there are Qian and Lang.

sentences.zh: 終考功郎中。

translations.literal: He ended as Director in the Ministry of Personnel's merit office.
translations.idiomatic: He ended his career as Director in the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 附 司空曙曙字文初，廣平人。

translations.literal: Appended — Sikong Shu: Shu, styled Wenchu, a native of Guangping.
translations.idiomatic: Appended biography: Sikong Shu, courtesy name Wenchu, a native of Guangping.

sentences.zh: 從韋臯於劍南，終虞部郎中。

translations.literal: He followed Wei Gao in Jiannan; he ended as Director in the Ministry of Works.
translations.idiomatic: He served under Wei Gao in Jiannan and eventually became Director in the Ministry of Works.

sentences.zh: 附 苗發發，晉卿子，終都官員外郎。

translations.literal: Appended — Miao Fa: Fa, son of Miao Jinqing; he ended as Outer Adjunct in the Ministry of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: Appended biography: Miao Fa, son of Miao Jinqing; he ended as Outer Adjunct in the Ministry of Justice.

sentences.zh: 峒終右補闕，湋右拾遺，審侍御史。

translations.literal: Tong ended as Right Supplementation Reminder; Wei ended as Right Admonition Reminder; Shen was Aide Censor.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Tong ended as Right Supplementation Reminder, Geng Wei as Right Admonition Reminder, and Xiahou Shen as Aide Censor.

sentences.zh: 附 李端端，趙州人。

translations.literal: Appended — Li Duan: Duan, a native of Zhao Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Appended biography: Li Duan, a native of Zhao Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 始，郭曖尚昇平公主，主賢明有才思，尤招納士，故端等多從曖游。

translations.literal: At the beginning, Guo Ai had married Princess Shengping; the princess was wise, enlightened, and gifted in thought, especially fond of gathering and welcoming scholars, and so Duan and the others often followed Ai in his associations.
translations.idiomatic: Early in his career, Guo Ai had married Princess Shengping, who was intelligent and talented and especially fond of gathering scholars about her; and so Duan and the others often kept company with Ai.

sentences.zh: 曖嘗進官，大集客，端賦詩最工，錢起曰：「素爲之，請賦起姓。」

translations.literal: Ai once presented himself at court and gathered many guests on a great scale; Duan's composed poem was most accomplished; Qian Qi said: "I have always composed for this; please compose on the surname Qi.
translations.idiomatic: On one occasion when Ai went to court and gathered a large company of guests, Duan's poem was judged the finest; Qian Qi said, "I have always been the one to compose on these occasions—now please compose on my surname, Qi.

sentences.zh: 端立獻一章，又工於前，客乃服，主賜帛百。

translations.literal: Duan immediately stood forth and presented one piece; it was again more accomplished than before; the guests then submitted; the princess bestowed a hundred bolts of silk.
translations.idiomatic: Duan at once rose and presented a new poem, finer still than the first; the guests were convinced, and the princess rewarded him with a hundred bolts of silk.

sentences.zh: 後移疾江南，終杭州司馬。

translations.literal: Later, claiming illness, he moved to Jiangnan; he ended as Military Adjunct of Hang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Later he retired to Jiangnan on grounds of illness and eventually died as Military Adjunct of Hang Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 歐陽詹歐陽詹字行周，泉州晉江人。

translations.literal: Ouyang Zhan — Ouyang Zhan, styled Xingzhou, a native of Jinjiang in Quan Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Ouyang Zhan, courtesy name Xingzhou, was a native of Jinjiang in Quan Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 其先皆爲本州州佐、縣令。

translations.literal: His forebears had all been prefectural aides and county magistrates in that prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: His ancestors had all served as prefectural aides and county magistrates in Quanzhou.

sentences.zh: 閩越地肥衍，有山泉禽魚，雖能通文書吏事，不肯北宦。

translations.literal: Min and Yue lands were rich and fertile, with mountain springs, birds, and fish; though they could manage written documents and clerkly duties, they were unwilling to take northern office.
translations.idiomatic: Min and Yue was fertile country rich in mountain springs, wild birds, and fish; though its people could manage documents and official business, they were reluctant to seek appointment in the north.

sentences.zh: 及常袞罷宰相爲觀察使，始擇縣鄕秀民能文辭者，與爲賓主鈞禮，觀游饗集必與，里人矜耀，故其俗稍相勸仕。

translations.literal: When Chang Gun left the post of chief minister and became Surveillance Commissioner, he for the first time selected outstanding local men from townships and districts who were skilled in literary composition, treated them as guest and host with equal courtesy, and always included them in touring, feasting, and gatherings; the villages took pride and showed off, and so the custom gradually encouraged one another toward office.
translations.idiomatic: When Chang Gun left the chief ministership to become Surveillance Commissioner, he began selecting talented local men skilled in letters, treating them as equals in guest-and-host ceremony, and always including them in his tours, banquets, and gatherings. Villagers took pride in this, and the local custom gradually began to encourage men to seek office.

sentences.zh: 初，詹與羅山甫同隱潘湖，往見袞，袞奇之。

translations.literal: At first Zhan and Luo Shanfu together lived in seclusion at Pan Lake; they went to see Gun, and Gun considered him extraordinary.
translations.idiomatic: Early on Zhan and Luo Shanfu lived in seclusion together at Pan Lake; when they called on Chang Gun, he was struck by Zhan's talent.

sentences.zh: 辭歸，泛舟飲餞。

translations.literal: When taking leave to return, [Gun] sailed a boat and set out drinks to see them off.
translations.idiomatic: When they took their leave, Chang Gun saw them off with a boat excursion and a parting feast.

sentences.zh: 舉進士，與韓愈、李觀、李絳、崔羣、王涯、馮宿、庾承宣聯第，皆天下選，時稱「龍虎榜」。

translations.literal: Entering the jinshi examination, he passed in the same cohort as Han Yu, Li Guan, Li Jiang, Cui Qun, Wang Ya, Feng Su, and Yu ChengXuan; all were chosen men from throughout the realm, and the age called them "the Dragon-Tiger Register."
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination in the same year as Han Yu, Li Guan, Li Jiang, Cui Qun, Wang Ya, Feng Su, and Yu ChengXuan—a cohort of men chosen from across the empire, known in its day as the "Dragon-and-Tiger Register."

sentences.zh: 閩人第進士，自詹始。

translations.literal: A native of Min passing the jinshi examination began with Zhan.
translations.idiomatic: Zhan was the first native of Fujian ever to pass the jinshi examination.

sentences.zh: 詹事父母孝，與朋友信義。

translations.literal: Zhan in serving his parents was filial; with friends he was faithful and righteous.
translations.idiomatic: In serving his parents he was filial; in friendship he was loyal and true.

sentences.zh: 其文章切深，回復明辯。

translations.literal: His writings were keen and profound, circumspect and clearly argumentative.
translations.idiomatic: His essays were incisive and profound, layered and lucid in argument.

sentences.zh: 與愈友善。

translations.literal: He was good friends with Han Yu.
translations.idiomatic: He and Han Yu were close friends.

sentences.zh: 詹先爲國子監四門助教，率其徒伏闕下，舉愈博士。

translations.literal: Zhan was first Four Gates Assistant Instructor at the Directorate of Education; leading his disciples he prostrated himself below the palace gate and recommended Han Yu for the doctorate.
translations.idiomatic: While serving as Four Gates Assistant Instructor at the Directorate of Education, Zhan led his students in kneeling before the palace gate to recommend Han Yu for the doctorate.

sentences.zh: 卒，年四十餘。

translations.literal: He died, aged a little more than forty.
translations.idiomatic: He died in his early forties.

sentences.zh: 崔羣哭之甚，愈爲詹哀辭，自書以遺羣。

translations.literal: Cui Qun wept for him exceedingly; Han Yu composed a lament for Zhan, personally wrote it out and gave it to Qun.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Qun mourned him deeply; Han Yu composed a dirge for Zhan, copied it out in his own hand, and sent it to Qun.

sentences.zh: 初，徐晦舉進士不中，詹數稱之，明年髙第，仕爲福建觀察使。

translations.literal: At first Xu Hui entered the jinshi examination but did not pass; Zhan repeatedly praised him; the next year he placed at the top; he served as Surveillance Commissioner of Fujian.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Hui had first failed the jinshi examination, but Zhan repeatedly praised him; the following year Xu placed at the top of the list, and eventually became Surveillance Commissioner of Fujian.

sentences.zh: 語及詹，必流涕。

translations.literal: Whenever he spoke of Zhan, he invariably shed tears.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever he spoke of Zhan, he wept.

sentences.zh: 從子 秬從子秬，字降之，亦工爲文。

translations.literal: Nephew: Ju — nephew Ju, styled Jiangzhi, also skilled at composing writings.
translations.idiomatic: Nephew: Ouyang Ju, courtesy name Jiangzhi, was also skilled as a writer.

sentences.zh: 陸洿自右拾遺除司勳郎中，棄官隱呉中，詔召之，既在道，秬遺書讓出處之遽，洿不至，還．秬名益聞。

translations.literal: Lu Hu, from Right Admonition Reminder, was appointed Director in the Ministry of Personnel; he abandoned office and lived in seclusion in Wu lands; an edict summoned him; already on the road, Ju sent a letter remonstrating against the haste of his going out and returning to office; Hu did not arrive; returned. Ju's name grew ever more renowned.
translations.idiomatic: When Lu Hu was promoted from Right Admonition Reminder to Director in the Ministry of Personnel, he resigned and went into seclusion in the Wu region; an edict summoned him back, but while he was already en route Ju sent a letter reproaching him for the precipitous manner of his return to office. Hu never arrived; he turned back—and Ju's reputation rose higher still.

sentences.zh: 開成中，擢進士第，而里人蕭本妄言與貞獻太后近屬，恩寵赫然，秬恥之。

translations.literal: In the Kaicheng era he was promoted by passing the jinshi examination; yet a fellow townsman, Xiao Ben, falsely claimed kinship with Empress Zhenxian; favor and patronage were conspicuous; Ju was ashamed of it.
translations.idiomatic: During the Kaicheng era he passed the jinshi examination, but a fellow townsman named Xiao Ben falsely claimed close kinship with Empress Zhenxian and basked in conspicuous imperial favor—a spectacle that filled Ju with shame.

sentences.zh: 會澤潞劉從諫表秬在幕府，秬爲辯質本之偽，本終得罪。

translations.literal: When Liu Congjian of Zelu memorialized that Ju was in his military staff, Ju argued and proved the falsity of Ben; Ben in the end was punished with a crime.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Congjian of Zelu reported that Ju was serving on his staff, Ju exposed the falsity of Ben's claim; Ben was eventually punished.

sentences.zh: 其子稹拒命，秬方休假還家，稹表斥損時政，或言秬爲之，詔流崖州，賜死。

translations.literal: His son Zhen defied commands; Ju was just on leave returning home; Zhen memorialized condemning and denigrating current policy; some said Ju had done it; an edict exiled him to Yazhou and ordered death by grace.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Congjian's son Zhen rebelled against imperial orders, Ju happened to be home on leave; Zhen submitted memorials attacking current policy, and some claimed Ju had written them. An edict exiled Ju to Yazhou and commanded that he be granted death.

sentences.zh: 臨刑，色不橈，爲書徧謝故人，自誌墓，人皆憐之。

translations.literal: Facing execution, his color did not waver; he wrote letters everywhere to thank old friends, inscribed his own tomb epitaph; everyone pitied him.
translations.idiomatic: At the hour of execution his bearing did not falter; he wrote letters of farewell to old friends throughout and composed his own tomb inscription—and all who knew of it mourned him.

sentences.zh: 李賀李賀字長吉，系出鄭王後。

translations.literal: Li He — Li He, styled Changji, traced his lineage to the Prince of Zheng's descendants.
translations.idiomatic: Li He, courtesy name Changji, was descended from the line of the Prince of Zheng.

sentences.zh: 七歳能辭章，韓愈、皇甫湜始聞未信，過其家，使賀賦詩，援筆輒就如素構，自目曰髙軒過，二人大驚，自是有名。

translations.literal: At seven sui he could compose literary pieces; Han Yu and Huangfu Shi at first heard and did not believe; they passed his home, had He compose a poem; taking brush he immediately completed it as if long prepared; he himself entitled it "A Lofty Carriage Passes By"; the two men were greatly astonished; from then on he had a name.
translations.idiomatic: At the age of seven he could already compose polished prose; when Han Yu and Huangfu Shi first heard of this they did not believe it, so they called at his home and asked the boy to compose a poem on the spot. He took up the brush and finished at once, as though the verses had been fully formed in his mind beforehand; he titled the poem "A Lofty Carriage Passes By." The two men were astonished, and from that day his fame was made.

sentences.zh: 爲人纖瘦，通眉，長指爪，能疾書。

translations.literal: As a person he was slender and thin, with joined eyebrows and long fingernails, able to write swiftly.
translations.idiomatic: He was slight and gaunt in build, with conjoined eyebrows and long fingernails, and wrote with exceptional speed.

sentences.zh: 毎旦日出，騎弱馬，從小奚奴，背古錦囊，遇所得，書投囊中。

translations.literal: Every morning at sunrise he rode a weak horse, followed by a little servant boy, carrying on his back an ancient brocade pouch; whatever he obtained he wrote and cast into the pouch.
translations.idiomatic: Each morning at sunrise he would ride a weary horse with a young servant boy trailing behind, an old brocade satchel on his back; whenever inspiration struck, he would scribble the lines and toss them into the bag.

sentences.zh: 未始先立題然後爲詩，如它人牽合程課者。

translations.literal: He never first established a topic and then composed poetry, as other people did when forced to fit assignments and scheduled lessons.
translations.idiomatic: He never composed to a set topic in advance, as others did when bending their work to examination assignments.

sentences.zh: 及暮歸，足成之。

translations.literal: When evening came and he returned, he would fully complete them.
translations.idiomatic: Only when he returned home at dusk would he polish the scraps into finished poems.

sentences.zh: 非大醉、弔喪日率如此。

translations.literal: Unless on days of great drunkenness or mourning visits, as a rule it was thus.
translations.idiomatic: On every day but those of heavy drinking or funeral attendance, his routine was always the same.

sentences.zh: 過亦不甚省。

translations.literal: When passing by he also did not much examine [them].
translations.idiomatic: Even then he rarely looked back over what he had written.

sentences.zh: 母使婢探囊中，見所書多，即怒曰：「是兒要嘔出心乃已耳。」

translations.literal: His mother had a maidservant probe the pouch; seeing the writings were many, she at once angrily said: "This boy intends to vomit out his heart before he will stop.
translations.idiomatic: His mother ordered a maid to search the pouch; when she found it overflowing with drafts, the mother cried out in anger, "This boy will not rest until he has vomited up his very heart!

sentences.zh: 以父名晉肅，不肯舉進士，愈爲作諱辨，然卒亦不就舉。

translations.literal: Because his father's name was Jinsu, he refused to enter the jinshi examination; Han Yu composed for him a memorial arguing against taboo; yet in the end he still did not take the examination.
translations.idiomatic: Because his father's name was Jinsu, he would not sit for the jinshi examination; Han Yu wrote a memorial on his behalf arguing that the name taboo should not apply, but He never took the examination in the end.

sentences.zh: 辭尚奇詭，所得皆驚邁，絶去翰墨畦逕，當時無能效者。

translations.literal: His phrasing prized the strange and uncanny; what he obtained was all startling and surpassing; he utterly departed from the furrows and paths of brush and ink; in his time none could imitate him.
translations.idiomatic: His language favored the strange and uncanny; his effects were startling and singular; he broke entirely from ordinary literary conventions, and none of his contemporaries could match him.

sentences.zh: 樂府數十篇，雲韶諸工皆合之絃管。

translations.literal: Several tens of yuefu pieces — all the artisans of the Cloud Harmony [ensemble] set them to string and pipe.
translations.idiomatic: Several dozen of his yuefu poems were set to music by the performers of the Cloud Harmony ensemble.

sentences.zh: 爲協律郎，卒，年二十七。

translations.literal: He served as Coordinator of Musical Harmony; he died, aged twenty-seven.
translations.idiomatic: He served as Coordinator of Musical Harmony and died at the age of twenty-seven.

sentences.zh: 與游者權璩、楊敬之、王恭元，毎譔著，時爲所取去。

translations.literal: Those who associated with him were Quan Xu, Yang Jingzhi, and Wang Gongyuan; whenever he composed and wrote, in his time [others] would take them away.
translations.idiomatic: His companions included Quan Xu, Yang Jingzhi, and Wang Gongyuan, who often made off with his freshly written pieces before he could keep them.

sentences.zh: 賀亦早世，故其詩歌世傳者鮮焉。

translations.literal: He also died young; and so the poems and songs of his that the world transmits are few.
translations.idiomatic: He too died young, and so few of his poems survive in circulation.

sentences.zh: 呉武陵呉武陵，信州人。

translations.literal: Wu Wuling — Wu Wuling, a native of Xin Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Wuling, a native of Xin Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 元和初，擢進士第。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Yuanhe reign he was promoted by passing the jinshi examination.
translations.idiomatic: In the early Yuanhe era he passed the jinshi examination.

sentences.zh: 淮西呉少陽聞其才，遣客鄭平邀之，將待以賓友，武陵不答。

translations.literal: Wu Shaoyang of Huai West heard of his talent, dispatched the guest Zheng Ping to invite him, intending to treat him as guest and friend; Wuling did not reply.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Shaoyang of Huai West, hearing of his talent, sent a client named Zheng Ping to invite him, intending to honor him as an honored guest—but Wuling gave no answer.

sentences.zh: 俄而少陽子元濟叛，武陵遺以書，自稱東呉王孫，曰：

translations.literal: Before long Shaoyang's son Yuanji rebelled; Wuling sent him a letter, calling himself a descendant of the kings of Eastern Wu, saying:
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward Shaoyang's son Yuanji rose in rebellion; Wuling sent him a letter, styling himself a descendant of the kings of Eastern Wu, which read:

sentences.zh: 「夫勢有不必得，事有不必疑，徒取暴逆之名，而殄物敗俗，不可謂智；

translations.literal: "Now, momentum sometimes need not be seized, affairs sometimes need not be doubted; vainly taking the name of violent rebellion, yet destroying things and ruining custom — this cannot be called wisdom;
translations.idiomatic: "A position is not always there for the taking, and a course of action is not always as doubtful as you think. To win only the name of a violent rebel while laying waste to goods and corrupting society—this cannot be called wisdom;

sentences.zh: 一日亡破，平生親愛連頭就戮，不可謂仁；

translations.literal: In one day ruin and destruction; all one's lifelong intimates and loved ones, heads severed together in slaughter — this cannot be called benevolence;
translations.idiomatic: When in a single day your house is destroyed, your closest kin and friends will fall one after another beneath the executioner's blade—this cannot be called benevolence;

sentences.zh: 支屬繁衍，因縁磨滅，先魂傷餒，不可謂孝；

translations.literal: Branch kin proliferate; through ties they are ground away and extinguished; the spirits of forebears wounded and starving — this cannot be called filial piety;
translations.idiomatic: Your extended clan is large and flourishing, yet through your act it will be ground to extinction; the shades of your ancestors will go hungry and wounded in the grave—this cannot be called filial piety;

sentences.zh: 數百里之内，拘若檻，常疑死於左右手，低回姑息，不可謂明。

translations.literal: Within several hundred li, confined as in a cage, constantly suspecting death at one's left and right hands, hesitating and indulgent — this cannot be called clear-sightedness.
translations.idiomatic: Within a radius of hundreds of li you will be penned up like a prisoner, always fearing death at the very hand that sustains you—hesitating, temporizing, indulging your fears. This cannot be called clarity.

sentences.zh: 且三皇以來，數千萬載，何有勃理亂常而能自畢者哉？

translations.literal: Moreover, since the Three Sovereigns, through tens of millions of years, has there ever been one who violently disturbed order and violated constants and yet could complete himself?
translations.idiomatic: Since the age of the Three Sovereigns, across tens of millions of years, who has ever violently overturned the natural order and still met a peaceful end?

sentences.zh: 貞元時，德宗以函容御天下，河北諸鎭專地不臣，朝廷資以爵號，桀黠者自謂得計，以反爲利，於是楊惠琳、劉闢、李錡、盧從史等又亂。

translations.literal: In the Zhenyuan era Dezong governed All Under Heaven with tolerance and forbearance; the various prefectures of Hebei monopolized territory and did not submit; the court supplied them with titles and ranks; the violent and cunning considered themselves to have found a scheme, taking rebellion as profit; and so Yang Huilin, Liu Pi, Li Qi, Lu Congshi, and others again rebelled.
translations.idiomatic: In the Zhenyuan era Emperor Dezong governed with forbearance; the military prefectures of Hebei held their territories and refused submission, while the court kept awarding them titles and offices. The shrewdest among them decided that rebellion paid—and so Yang Huilin, Liu Pi, Li Qi, Lu Congshi, and others rose in revolt again.

sentences.zh: 皇帝即位，赫然命偏師討之，盡伏其辜，所謂時也。

translations.literal: The Emperor upon ascending the throne, boldly ordered detachments to campaign against them; all submitted to their guilt; this is what is called the timely moment.
translations.idiomatic: When our emperor took the throne, he boldly dispatched punitive columns against them, and every culprit was brought to justice. This, sir, is what we call the right moment.

sentences.zh: 「日者，張太尉厭垣捍之勤，謝易、定爲國老，田尚書知慮絶俗，又以魏博來歸，幽、檀、滄、景皆爲信臣，然而與足下者，獨齊、趙耳。

translations.literal: "Recently, Grand Marshal Zhang wearied of the toil of defense on the walls; Xie took Yi and Ding as elders of the state; Minister of Works Tian's knowing counsel was beyond the common; moreover Weibo returned in submission; You, Tan, Cang, and Jing all became trusted ministers; yet those on the same footing as yourself are solely Qi and Zhao.
translations.idiomatic: "Not long ago Marshal Zhang grew weary of the endless burden of border defense; the old commanders of Yicheng and Dingzhou were honored as statesmen emeriti; Minister Tian's wisdom was matchless; Weibo has submitted again; Youzhou, Tanzhou, Cangzhou, and Jingzhou are all held by loyal commanders. Of all your potential allies, only Qi and Zhao remain.

sentences.zh: 夫齊安可爲恃哉？

translations.literal: Now, how can Qi be relied upon?
translations.idiomatic: But how can you rely on Qi at all?

sentences.zh: 徐壓其首，梁薄其翼，魏斮其脛，滑鍼其腹，淮南承其衝，分兵不足相救，全舉則曹、魯、東平非其有也。

translations.literal: Xu presses its head; Liang thins its wings; Wei hews its shins; Hua needles its belly; Huainan receives its charge; divided troops are insufficient to rescue one another; if fully deployed, then Cao, Lu, and Dongping would not be its to possess.
translations.idiomatic: Xuzhou presses on its head, Liangzhou thins its wings, Weibo hews at its shins, Huazhou pierces its belly, and Huainan stands ready to take the full shock of its fall. Divided forces cannot rescue one another; and if Qi commits everything it has, it will lose Cao, Lu, and Dongping besides.

sentences.zh: 彼何苦而自棄哉？

translations.literal: Why should they bitterly throw themselves away?
translations.idiomatic: Why would they suffer so only to destroy themselves?

sentences.zh: 若趙則固子耳。

translations.literal: As for Zhao, it is simply Zi.
translations.idiomatic: As for Zhao—it is merely your own son's domain, nothing more.

sentences.zh: 前日，主上以澤潞爲之導，既斥從史，姑赦罪，復爵祿之，天下之人欲討者十八，無何，殘丞相御史，朝廷以足下故，未加斧鉞也。

translations.literal: The other day, the sovereign took Zelu as its guide; having already dismissed Congshi, for the moment pardoned the crime and restored rank and emolument; men throughout the realm who wished to campaign numbered eighteen parts in ten; before long, maiming the chief minister and censor; the court because of yourself has not yet applied ax and halberd.
translations.idiomatic: Recently the emperor looked to Zelu as the model: Lu Congshi was removed, but for the time being his crimes were pardoned and his rank and stipend restored. Eighteen parts in ten of all who dwell under heaven wish to see you punished; yet after you maimed the chief minister and the censor, the court has still held back the axe and halberd—for your sake alone.

sentences.zh: 然則中山搏城之險，太原乘井陘之隘，燕徇樂壽，邢扼臨城，淸河絶其南，弓髙斷其北，孤雛腐鼠，求責不暇，又曷以救人哉？

translations.literal: Thus then Zhongshan holds fast to its walled fortifications' peril; Taiyuan rides the narrowness of Jingxing Pass; Yan spreads to Leshou; Xing chokes off Lincheng; Qinghe cuts off its south; Gonggao blocks its north — an orphaned chick and rotting rat, with demands for account not even having leisure — how moreover could one save others?
translations.idiomatic: Zhongshan will hold its walled strongholds at all costs; Taiyuan will seal the Jingxing Pass; Yan will march on Leshou; Xingzhou will choke the crossing at Lincheng; Qinghe will sever your southern routes and Gonggao your northern ones. You will be a helpless wretch with enemies pressing in from every side—barely able to answer for yourself, let alone rescue anyone else.

sentences.zh: 二鎭不敢動亦明矣，足下何待而窮處邪？

translations.literal: That the two prefectures dare not stir is also clear; what do you await, sir, in this desperate position?
translations.idiomatic: It is plain enough that neither of those two commands will stir on your behalf. What, then, are you still waiting for in this desperate corner?

sentences.zh: 「昔僕之師裴道明嘗言：『唐家二百載有中興主，當其時，佷傲者盡滅，河、湟之地復矣。』

translations.literal: "In the past my teacher Pei Daoming once said: 'In the Tang family's two hundred years there will be a restoration emperor; at that time, the violent and arrogant will all perish, and the lands of He and Huang will be recovered.
translations.idiomatic: "My former teacher Pei Daoming once said: 'Through its two hundred years the Tang will produce an emperor of restoration. When he arrives, every arrogant rebel will be destroyed and the lands of the Yellow and Huang Rivers will return to the realm.

sentences.zh: 今天子英武任賢，同符太宗，寬仁厚物，有玄宗之度，罰無貸罪，賞無遺功。

translations.literal: The present Son of Heaven is heroic and martial, employs the worthy, matches Taizong, is generous and benevolent and treats things with depth, possesses Xuanzong's magnanimity, in punishment does not pardon guilt, in reward does not omit merit.
translations.idiomatic: Our emperor today is brave and martial, delights in appointing worthy men—he matches Emperor Taizong in talent and Emperor Xuanzong in magnanimity. He pardons no guilt in punishment and leaves no merit unrewarded.

sentences.zh: 諸侯豢齊、趙以稔其釁，帥築室礪兵，進窺房、蔡，屯田繼漕，前鋒扼喉，後陣撫背，左排右掖，其幾何而不踣邪？

translations.literal: The feudal lords feed Qi and Zhao to ripen their provocation; the marshal builds dwellings and sharpens weapons, advances to peer at Fang and Cai, garrison-farming follows grain transport, vanguard chokes the throat, rear formation strokes the back, left files and right flank — how long before they do not fall?
translations.idiomatic: The imperial commanders are fattening Qi and Zhao until rebellion ripens, building fortifications and sharpening arms, pressing toward Fang and Cai. They sow garrison fields and keep the grain boats moving—the vanguard at your throat, the rear columns at your back, forces closing in from every side. How long before you collapse?

sentences.zh: 「足下勿謂部曲勿我欺，人心與足下一也。

translations.literal: "Do not, sir, think that your subordinates will not deceive you — the hearts of men are the same as yours, sir.
translations.idiomatic: "Do not suppose your men would never turn on you. Their hearts work just like yours.

sentences.zh: 足下反天子，人亦欲反足下。

translations.literal: If you, sir, rebel against the Son of Heaven, others also wish to rebel against you.
translations.idiomatic: If you rebel against the emperor, your men will want to rebel against you.

sentences.zh: 易地而論，則嬰兇橫之命，不若奉大君官守矣。

translations.literal: Exchanging places and discussing, then clinging to a violent and tyrannical command is not as good as serving the great lord's official charge.
translations.idiomatic: Put yourself in your men's place: clinging to a brutal tyrant's orders is less attractive than holding legitimate office under the emperor.

sentences.zh: 枕戈持矛，死不得地，不若坐兼爵命而保胤嗣矣。

translations.literal: Pillowing on spears and grasping lances, dying without ground for burial, is not as good as sitting and joining titles and commands while preserving posterity.
translations.idiomatic: Sleeping with a spear for a pillow and dying without even ground for burial—surely that is worse than keeping your titles and safeguarding your heirs in peace.

sentences.zh: 足下苟能挺知幾之烈，莫若發一介，籍士馬土疆，歸之有司。

translations.literal: If you, sir, can uphold the valor of knowing the moment, none is better than sending a single messenger, registering troops, horses, land, and territory, and returning them to the officials.
translations.idiomatic: If you have the courage to read the turning point, send a single envoy—register your soldiers, horses, and territory, and deliver them to the imperial authorities.

sentences.zh: 上以覆載之仁，必保納足下，滌垢洗瑕，以倡四海，將校官屬不失寵且貴。

translations.literal: Above, with heaven-and-earth-covering benevolence, will surely protect and receive you, sir, washing away filth and cleansing blemishes, to lead the four seas; generals, officers, and attendants will not lose favor and eminence.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor's mercy is as wide as heaven and earth. He will surely accept you, wash away your stains, and hold you up as an example to the empire. Your officers and staff will keep their honors and rank.

sentences.zh: 何哉？

translations.literal: Why?
translations.idiomatic: Why?

sentences.zh: 爲國者不以纖惡蓋大善也。

translations.literal: One who governs a state does not let a tiny evil cover a great good.
translations.idiomatic: A state does not allow small faults to eclipse great merits.

sentences.zh: 且貳而伐，服而捨，寵榮可厚，骨肉可保，何獨不爲哉？

translations.literal: Moreover, those who are disloyal are punished in war, those who submit are spared; favor and glory can be thick, flesh-and-blood kin can be preserved — why alone not act?
translations.idiomatic: The dynasty punishes rebels but spares those who submit. Honors can be heaped upon you; your family can be kept safe. Why would you alone refuse?

sentences.zh: 「三州至狹也，萬國至廣也，力不相侔，判然可知。

translations.literal: "Three prefectures are extremely narrow, ten thousand states are extremely broad; strength does not match, clearly distinguishable and knowable.
translations.idiomatic: "Your three prefectures are tiny; the empire is vast. The disparity in power is obvious.

sentences.zh: 假使官軍百敗，而行陣未嘗乏，足下一敗則成禽矣。

translations.literal: Suppose the government army loses a hundred times, yet its battle lines never lack; one defeat for you, sir, and you become a captive.
translations.idiomatic: Even if the imperial army lost a hundred battles, its ranks would never run dry—but one defeat for you and you are finished.

sentences.zh: 夫一壯士不能當十夫者，以其左右前後咸敵也，矧以一卒欲當百人哉！

translations.literal: That one strong man cannot match ten men is because those to his left, right, front, and rear are all enemies — how much more if one soldier wishes to match a hundred men!
translations.idiomatic: A single brave man cannot hold off ten because enemies surround him on every side—so how could one soldier stand against a hundred?

sentences.zh: 昏迷不返，諸侯之師集城下，環壘刳塹，灌以流潦，主將怨攜，士卒崩離，田儋、呂興發於肘腋。

translations.literal: Dazed and not returning, the feudal lords' armies gather below the walls, encircle the ramparts and dig moats, flood with flowing water, the commander resentful and estranged, soldiers collapsing and scattering, Tian Dan and Lu Xing erupt from elbow and armpit.
translations.idiomatic: If you persist in your delusion, the allied armies will ring your walls, trench your ramparts, and flood your defenses. Your commander will turn against you, your troops will break and flee, and mutiny will burst out at your very side—as Tian Dan and Lu Xing once did.

sentences.zh: 屍不得裹，宗不得祀，臣僕以爲誡，子孫所不祖，生爲暗愎之人。

translations.literal: Corpses cannot be wrapped, the ancestral temple cannot be sacrificed to; ministers and servants take it as a warning, descendants do not enshrine them, living as obstinate and perverse men.
translations.idiomatic: Your corpse will go unshrouded and your ancestors unhonored. Servants will point to you as a warning; your descendants will not claim you. You will live as a man of blind stubbornness.

sentences.zh: 沒爲幽憂之鬼，何其痛哉！」

translations.literal: After death becoming a ghost of hidden sorrow — how painful!"
translations.idiomatic: In death you will become a restless ghost in the dark—what agony!"

sentences.zh: 元濟得書不悟。

translations.literal: Yuanji received the letter but did not comprehend.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanji received the letter but took no heed.

sentences.zh: 會裴度東討，而韓愈爲司馬，武陵勸愈爲度謀：「取中官常所不快者爲監軍，歸素所快者於内，爲吾地以傾諸侯，出帛百萬以給士大夫，則孰不爲丞相之人？

translations.literal: When Pei Du campaigned east and Han Yu served as marshal, Wuling urged Han Yu to advise Du: "Take the eunuch officials the emperor is usually displeased with as army supervisors, return those the emperor usually favors to the inner [palace], secure territory for us to overturn the feudal lords, disburse a million bolts of silk to supply the scholar-officials — then who would not become the chief minister's man?
translations.idiomatic: When Pei Du marched east and Han Yu served as his chief of staff, Wuling urged Han to counsel Du: "Appoint eunuchs the emperor dislikes as army supervisors, recall his favorites to the inner palace, carve out a base from which to topple the military governors, and distribute a million bolts of silk among the literati—then who would not be the chief minister's man?

sentences.zh: 然後分三大將環賊而屯，明斥候，牛酒髙會，潛以實期授瀕蔡諸將，而以三期紿賊，令辯士持尺書劫元濟及將士約降，彼無所竄謀矣。」

translations.literal: Then divide three great generals to encircle the rebels and encamp, clearly post scouts, hold feasts with oxen and wine, secretly give the real deadline to the commanders on the Cai border, yet deceive the rebels with a three-period deadline, send eloquent envoys bearing letters to coerce Yuanji and his officers and soldiers into surrender — they would have nowhere to flee or plot."
translations.idiomatic: Then station three great generals in a ring around the rebels, set out clear pickets, hold lavish feasts—and secretly give the commanders on the Cai frontier the real date of attack while telling the rebels it will come in three months. Send skilled negotiators with letters pressing Yuanji and his men to surrender, and they will have nowhere left to run or scheme."

sentences.zh: 時度部分已定，故不見用。

translations.literal: At the time Du's deployment was already settled, so it was not adopted.
translations.idiomatic: By then Du's battle plan was already fixed, so the scheme was not used.

sentences.zh: 元濟未破數月，武陵自硤石望東南，氣如旗鼓矛楯，皆顛倒橫斜。

translations.literal: Several months before Yuanji's defeat, Wuling from Xiashi gazed toward the southeast; qi like banners, drums, spears, and shields, all inverted and slanting.
translations.idiomatic: Months before Yuanji fell, Wuling looked southeast from Xiashi and saw vapors shaped like banners, drums, spears, and shields—all tilted and awry.

sentences.zh: 少選，黃白氣出西北，盤蜿相交。

translations.literal: After a little while, yellow and white qi emerged from the northwest, coiling and intersecting.
translations.idiomatic: Shortly afterward yellow and white vapors rose from the northwest, twisting and interweaving.

sentences.zh: 武陵告愈曰：「今西北王師所在，氣黃白，喜象也。

translations.literal: Wuling told Han Yu: "Now the northwest is where the royal army stands; the qi is yellow and white — an auspicious sign.
translations.idiomatic: Wuling told Han Yu: "The imperial army lies to the northwest, and the vapors there are yellow and white—an omen of victory.

sentences.zh: 敗氣爲賊，日直木，舉其盈數，不閲六十日，賊必亡。

translations.literal: The qi of defeat belongs to the rebels; the day corresponds to wood; counting its full number, within no more than sixty days the rebels will perish.
translations.idiomatic: The losing vapors belong to the rebels. Today the day-stem is wood; count out the full cycle and the rebels will fall within sixty days.

sentences.zh: 夫天見其祥，宜脩事應之。

translations.literal: Heaven shows this auspicious sign; one should cultivate affairs to respond to it.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven has shown its sign—you should act to meet it.

sentences.zh: 且洄曲守將急緩不可使，呉城賊將趙曄詐而輕，若以兵誘之，伏以待，一舉可奪其城，則右臂斷矣。」

translations.literal: Moreover the Huiqu garrison commander cannot be trusted whether in urgency or slack; the rebel commander Zhao Ye at Wucheng is deceitful and light — if troops lure him, lie in ambush and wait, in one stroke the city can be seized, then the right arm is severed."
translations.idiomatic: The garrison commander at Huiqu is unreliable in crisis or calm alike; the rebel Zhao Ye at Wucheng is cunning and rash. Lure him out, lay an ambush, and you can take the city in a single stroke—cutting off their right arm."

sentences.zh: 武陵之奇譎類如此。

translations.literal: Wuling's schemes were all eccentric like this.
translations.idiomatic: Wuling's stratagems were all as ingenious and unorthodox as this.

sentences.zh: 長慶初，竇易直以戸部侍郎判度支，表武陵主鹽北邊。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Changqing, Dou Yizhi, as Vice Minister of Revenue overseeing the Finance Commission, memorialized to appoint Wuling to manage salt on the northern frontier.
translations.idiomatic: In the early Changqing era Dou Yizhi, serving as Vice Minister of Revenue with oversight of the Finance Commission, recommended Wuling to administer salt on the northern frontier.

sentences.zh: 易直以不職，薄其遇。

translations.literal: Yizhi, for incompetence, reduced his remuneration.
translations.idiomatic: Yizhi cut his salary for poor performance.

sentences.zh: 會表置和糴貯備使，擇郎中爲之。

translations.literal: When a memorial was submitted to establish a Commissioner for Harmonious Purchase and Storage Reserves, a director-level official was chosen for the post.
translations.idiomatic: When a memorial proposed creating a Commissioner for Harmonious Purchase and Reserve Storage, a bureau director was selected for the office.

sentences.zh: 武陵諫曰：「今縁邊膏壤，鞠爲榛𣏌，父母妻子不相活。

translations.literal: Wuling remonstrated: "Now along the frontier the fertile lands have become thorn scrub; parents, wives, and children cannot keep one another alive.
translations.idiomatic: Wuling remonstrated: "On the frontier the rich soil has turned to wasteland; families cannot even keep themselves alive.

sentences.zh: 前在朔方，度支米價四十，而無踰月積，皆先取商人，而後求牒還都受錢。

translations.literal: Previously at Shuofang, Finance Commission rice cost forty [cash], yet there was never more than a month's accumulation; all first took from merchants, then sought documents to return to the capital and receive payment.
translations.idiomatic: At Shuofang the Finance Commission paid forty cash per bushel of rice, yet never kept a month's supply on hand—it always requisitioned grain from merchants first and only later sent documents to the capital for reimbursement.

sentences.zh: 脱有寇薄城，不三旬便當餓死，何所取財而云和糴哉？

translations.literal: If bandits press the walls, within less than thirty days people will starve to death — from what source take wealth and speak of harmonious purchase?
translations.idiomatic: If raiders threaten the walls, the garrison will starve within a month. Where is the grain for this so-called harmonious purchase?

sentences.zh: 天下不治，病權不歸有司也。

translations.literal: When All Under Heaven is not well governed, the disease is that authority does not return to the regular offices.
translations.idiomatic: When the realm falls into disorder, the root cause is that power no longer rests with the proper agencies.

sentences.zh: 鹽鐵、度支一戸部郎事，今三分其務，吏萬員，財賦日蹙。

translations.literal: Salt and iron, and the Finance Commission, were the business of one Household Ministry director; now the duties are split three ways, officials number ten thousand, and revenue grows tighter by the day.
translations.idiomatic: Salt, iron, and fiscal affairs were once the work of a single Household Ministry director. Now the duties are divided three ways, the bureaucracy swells to ten thousand officers, and revenue grows tighter every day.

sentences.zh: 西北邊院官，皆御史、員外郎爲之。

translations.literal: Officials of the northwestern frontier bureaus are all appointed from among censors and vice directors.
translations.idiomatic: Northwestern frontier offices are all staffed by censors and vice directors.

sentences.zh: 始命若責可信，今又加使權其務，是御史、員外久於事，返不可信也。

translations.literal: At first the appointments seemed trustworthy; now adding commissioners with authority over the duties — censors and vice directors who have long handled affairs are in turn deemed untrustworthy.
translations.idiomatic: At first those appointments seemed reliable; now you add commissioners with special authority over the same duties—meaning the censors and vice directors who have managed these affairs for years are suddenly not to be trusted.

sentences.zh: 今更旬月，又將以郎中之爲不可信。

translations.literal: Change it again in another month or two, and bureau directors too will be deemed untrustworthy.
translations.idiomatic: Wait another month or two and bureau directors will be deemed untrustworthy as well.

sentences.zh: 即更時歳，明公之爲，亦又不可信。

translations.literal: Change again with the seasons and years, and even your excellency's own conduct will again be untrustworthy.
translations.idiomatic: Give it another year and even your own judgment will be called into question.

sentences.zh: 上下相阻，一國交疑，誰爲可信者？

translations.literal: Superiors and subordinates obstruct one another; the whole state exchanges suspicion — who is trustworthy?
translations.idiomatic: Superiors and subordinates block one another; the whole court grows mutual suspicion—who, then, can be trusted?

sentences.zh: 況一使之建，胥徒走卒殆百輩，督責騰呼，數千里爲不寧。

translations.literal: Moreover, once one commissioner is established, runners and attendants number nearly a hundred; supervision, demands, and clamor unsettle thousands of li.
translations.idiomatic: Worse, each new commissioner brings nearly a hundred runners and clerks in his train; their demands and shouting disturb the frontier for thousands of li.

sentences.zh: 誠欲邊隅完實，獨募浮民，徙罪人，發沃土，何必加使而增吏也？」

translations.literal: If one truly wishes the border regions complete and solid, simply recruit floating population, relocate convicts, and open fertile soil — why must one add commissioners and increase officials?"
translations.idiomatic: If you truly want strong border defenses, recruit landless settlers, relocate convicts, and cultivate fertile ground—why add commissioners and swell the bureaucracy?"

sentences.zh: 易直不納。

translations.literal: Yizhi did not accept it.
translations.idiomatic: Yizhi did not heed the advice.

sentences.zh: 久之，入爲太學博士。

translations.literal: After a long while, he entered [the capital] as Erudite of the Grand Academy.
translations.idiomatic: After some time he was recalled to the capital as Erudite of the Grand Academy.

sentences.zh: 大和初，禮部侍郎崔郾試進士東都，公卿咸祖道長樂，武陵最後至，謂郾曰：「君方爲天子求奇材，敢獻所益。」

translations.literal: At the beginning of Dahe, Vice Minister of Rites Cui Yan tested metropolitan graduates at the eastern capital; nobles and ministers all escorted the road at Changle; Wuling arrived last and said to Yan: "Your lordship is seeking extraordinary talent for the Son of Heaven — I venture to offer what may benefit you."
translations.idiomatic: In the early Dahe era Vice Minister of Rites Cui Yan held the metropolitan examination in the eastern capital. High officials lined the road at Changle to see him off. Wuling arrived last and said to Yan: "You are selecting extraordinary talent for the emperor—I have something to contribute."

sentences.zh: 因出袖中書搢笏，郾讀之，乃杜牧所賦阿房宮，辭既警拔，而武陵音吐鴻暢，坐客大驚。

translations.literal: Thereupon he produced a book from his sleeve and inserted it in his tablet; Yan read it — it was Du Mu's Ode to the Epang Palace; the language was startlingly elevated, and Wuling's voice was resonant and fluent; the seated guests were greatly astonished.
translations.idiomatic: He drew a scroll from his sleeve and handed it over. Yan read it—it was Du Mu's Ode to the Epang Palace. The prose was dazzling, and Wuling recited it in a ringing voice that astonished everyone present.

sentences.zh: 武陵請曰：「牧方試有司，請以第一人處之。」

translations.literal: Wuling requested: "Mu is now undergoing examination by the officials — please place him first."
translations.idiomatic: Wuling pressed him: "Du Mu is sitting the examination now—rank him first."

sentences.zh: 郾謝已得其人。

translations.literal: Yan apologized that he already had his man.
translations.idiomatic: Yan replied that he had already chosen his top candidate.

sentences.zh: 至第五，郾未對，武陵勃然曰：「不爾，宜以賦見還。」

translations.literal: When it came to fifth place, Yan had not answered; Wuling suddenly said: "If not, the composition ought to be returned."
translations.idiomatic: At the fifth-place ranking Yan still had not responded. Wuling flushed with anger: "If you will not, then return the essay."

sentences.zh: 郾曰：「如教。」

translations.literal: Yan said: "As you instruct."
translations.idiomatic: Yan said: "As you say."

sentences.zh: 牧果異等。

translations.literal: Mu indeed received a distinguished grade.
translations.idiomatic: Du Mu indeed received the highest honors.

sentences.zh: 後出爲韶州刺史，以贓貶潘州司戸參軍，卒。

translations.literal: Later he went out as Prefect of Shaozhou; for corruption he was demoted to Registrar of Panzhou and died.
translations.idiomatic: Later he served as prefect of Shaozhou; convicted of embezzlement he was demoted to registrar of Panzhou, where he died.

sentences.zh: 初，柳宗元謫永州，而武陵亦坐事流永州，宗元賢其人。

translations.literal: Initially, when Liu Zongyuan was banished to Yongzhou, Wuling also because of an affair was exiled to Yongzhou; Zongyuan esteemed the man.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Zongyuan was banished to Yongzhou, Wuling was exiled there for his own offense; Zongyuan admired him.

sentences.zh: 及爲柳州刺史，武陵北還，大爲裴度器遇。

translations.literal: When he became Prefect of Liuzhou, Wuling returned north and was greatly valued and treated well by Pei Du.
translations.idiomatic: When Zongyuan became prefect of Liuzhou, Wuling returned north and won Pei Du's high regard.

sentences.zh: 毎言宗元無子，説度曰：「西原蠻未平，柳州與賊犬牙，宜用武人以代宗元，使得優游江湖。」

translations.literal: He always said Zongyuan had no son, and told Du: "The western plain barbarians are not yet pacified; Liuzhou and the bandits are interlocked like dog teeth — a military man ought to replace Zongyuan, so that he may roam freely on rivers and lakes."
translations.idiomatic: He often noted that Zongyuan had no son and urged Du: "The western plain tribes are still unsettled; Liuzhou interlocks with rebel territory like interlocking teeth—a military man should replace Zongyuan so he can live out his days in peace by the rivers and lakes."

sentences.zh: 又遺工部侍郎孟簡書曰：「古稱一世三十年，子厚之斥十二年，殆半世矣。

translations.literal: He also sent a letter to Vice Minister of Works Meng Jian saying: "The ancients called one generation thirty years; Zihou's banishment has lasted twelve years — nearly half a lifetime.
translations.idiomatic: He also wrote Vice Minister of Works Meng Jian: "The ancients called thirty years one generation. Zihou has been in exile twelve years—nearly half a lifetime.

sentences.zh: 霆砰電射，天怒也，不能終朝。

translations.literal: Thunder crashes and lightning strikes — heaven's wrath — yet it cannot last the whole morning.
translations.idiomatic: Thunder crashes and lightning strikes—the wrath of heaven—but it cannot rage all morning.

sentences.zh: 聖人在上，安有畢世而怒人臣邪？

translations.literal: With a sage above, how could there be wrath against a minister lasting a whole lifetime?
translations.idiomatic: With a sage on the throne, would heaven's anger against one minister last an entire lifetime?

sentences.zh: 且程、劉、二韓皆已拔拭，或處大州劇職，獨子厚與猿鳥爲伍，誠恐霧露所嬰，則柳氏無後矣。」

translations.literal: Moreover Cheng, Liu, and the two Hans have all been lifted up; some hold great prefectures and heavy posts; only Zihou keeps company with apes and birds — truly I fear mist and dew will afflict him, then the Liu clan will have no posterity."
translations.idiomatic: Cheng, Liu, and the two Hans have all been restored—some to great prefectures and heavy offices—while Zihou alone keeps company with apes and birds. I fear disease will take him, and the Liu line will end."

sentences.zh: 度未及用，而宗元死。

translations.literal: Du had not yet acted when Zongyuan died.
translations.idiomatic: Du had not yet acted on the plea when Zongyuan died.

sentences.zh: 始，李愬節度唐、鄧，武陵薦李景儉、王湘健智沈敏，可表以自副，時號知人。

translations.literal: Initially, when Li Su commanded Tang and Deng, Wuling recommended Li Jingjian and Wang Xiangjian as intelligent, deep, and keen — fit to be listed as his own deputies; at the time he was called a knower of men.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when Li Su commanded Tang and Deng, Wuling recommended Li Jingjian and Wang Xiangjian as men of deep intelligence and quick judgment, worthy to serve as his deputies; at the time he was praised as a judge of talent.

sentences.zh: 李商隱李商隱字義山，懷州河内人。

translations.literal: Li Shangyin Li Shangyin, style name Yishan, was a man of Henei in Huai Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Li Shangyin, courtesy name Yishan, was a native of Henei in Huai Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 或言英國公世勣之裔孫。

translations.literal: Some say he was a descendant of Duke Ying of the state, Shiji.
translations.idiomatic: Some held that he was a descendant of Li Shiji, Duke Ying of the state.

sentences.zh: 令狐楚帥河陽，奇其文，使與諸子游。

translations.literal: Linghu Chu commanded Heyang and admired his writing, having him associate with his sons.
translations.idiomatic: When Linghu Chu governed Heyang he admired Li's literary talent and had him study alongside his sons.

sentences.zh: 楚徙天平、宣武，皆表署巡官，歳具資裝使隨計。

translations.literal: When Chu moved to Tianping and Xuanwu, in each case he listed him on memorials as touring official, yearly providing travel funds to follow the examination procession.
translations.idiomatic: When Chu transferred to Tianping and then Xuanwu, he repeatedly appointed Li as a staff touring official and each year supplied travel expenses for the metropolitan examination.

sentences.zh: 開成二年，髙鍇知貢舉，令狐綯雅善鍇，譽甚力，故擢進士第。

translations.literal: In the second year of Kaicheng, Gao Xia knew the examination; Linghu Tao was on excellent terms with Xia and praised him with great effort, so he was raised to metropolitan graduate rank.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Kaicheng, Gao Xia oversaw the examination. Linghu Tao was on close terms with Gao and pressed Li's case vigorously, and Li passed the metropolitan examination.

sentences.zh: 調弘農尉，以活獄忤觀察使孫簡，將罷去，會姚合代簡，諭使還官。

translations.literal: He was assigned as Registrar of Hongnong; for sparing prisoners from execution he offended Observation Commissioner Sun Jian and was about to be dismissed; when Yao He replaced Jian, he persuaded him to return to office.
translations.idiomatic: He was posted as registrar of Hongnong; when he spared prisoners from execution he offended Observation Commissioner Sun Jian and was nearly removed—but when Yao He replaced Jian, he persuaded Li to stay in office.

sentences.zh: 又試拔萃，中選。

translations.literal: He again tested for the Selection Examination and was chosen.
translations.idiomatic: He then passed the special selection examination.

sentences.zh: 王茂元鎭河陽，愛其才，表掌書記，以子妻之，得侍御史。

translations.literal: Wang Maoyuan commanded Heyang, loved his talent, memorialized him as chief secretary, gave him his daughter in marriage, and he received the post of Attending Censor.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Maoyuan governed Heyang, admired his talent, appointed him chief secretary, married his daughter to him, and secured him the post of attending censor.

sentences.zh: 茂元善李德裕，而牛、李黨人蚩謫商隱，以爲詭薄無行，共排笮之。

translations.literal: Maoyuan was on good terms with Li Deyu, while the Niu and Li faction men slandered Shangyin, deeming him deceitful, shallow, and without integrity, and jointly squeezed him out.
translations.idiomatic: Maoyuan was allied with Li Deyu, but the Niu-Li faction slandered Shangyin as deceitful and unprincipled and united to drive him out.

sentences.zh: 茂元死，來游京師，久不調，更依桂管觀察使鄭亞府爲判官。

translations.literal: When Maoyuan died, he came to roam the capital; long without appointment, he again relied on Guiguan Observation Commissioner Zheng Ya's office as judge.
translations.idiomatic: After Maoyuan died he went to the capital seeking office; long unemployed, he joined the staff of Guiguan Observation Commissioner Zheng Ya as judge.

sentences.zh: 亞謫循州，商隱從之，凡三年乃歸。

translations.literal: When Ya was banished to Xunzhou, Shangyin followed him; only after three years did he return.
translations.idiomatic: When Ya was banished to Xunzhou, Shangyin followed him and did not return for three years.

sentences.zh: 亞亦德裕所善，綯以爲忘家恩，放利偸合，謝不通。

translations.literal: Ya was also favored by Deyu; Tao considered him to have forgotten family kindness, sought profit and stole alliance, and refused communication.
translations.idiomatic: Ya was also a Deyu ally; Tao judged Shangyin to have forgotten Linghu family kindness and to have chased profit by switching sides, and broke off contact with him.

sentences.zh: 京兆尹盧弘止表爲府參軍，典牋奏。

translations.literal: Capital Prefect Lu Hongzhi memorialized him as army adjutant, in charge of memorial drafts.
translations.idiomatic: Capital Prefect Lu Hongzhi appointed him army adjutant in charge of memorial drafts.

sentences.zh: 綯當國，商隱歸窮自解，綯憾不置。

translations.literal: When Tao held state power, Shangyin wrote a humble self-defense; Tao resented him and would not let the matter rest.
translations.idiomatic: When Tao came to power Shangyin wrote a humble letter of self-defense; Tao resented him and would not let the matter drop.

sentences.zh: 弘止鎭徐州，表爲掌書記。

translations.literal: When Hongzhi commanded Xuzhou, he memorialized him as chief secretary.
translations.idiomatic: When Hongzhi governed Xuzhou he appointed Shangyin chief secretary.

sentences.zh: 久之，還朝，復干綯，乃補太學博士。

translations.literal: After a long while he returned to court, again petitioned Tao, and was then appointed Erudite of the Grand Academy.
translations.idiomatic: After some time he returned to court, petitioned Tao again, and was finally appointed Erudite of the Grand Academy.

sentences.zh: 柳仲郢節度劍南東川，辟判官，檢校工部員外郎。

translations.literal: Liu Zhongyi commanded Jiannan East Circuit, recruited him as judge, and he served as Acting Vice Director of the Ministry of Works.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Zhongyi, military governor of Jiannan East Circuit, recruited him as judge with the acting title of vice director in the Ministry of Works.

sentences.zh: 府罷，客滎陽，卒。

translations.literal: When the office was abolished, he lodged as a guest at Xingyang and died.
translations.idiomatic: When that post ended he stayed on as a guest at Xingyang, where he died.

sentences.zh: 商隱初爲文瑰邁奇古，及在令狐楚府，楚本工章奏，因授其學。

translations.literal: Initially Shangyin's writing was lofty, surpassing the ancient and strange; when he was in Linghu Chu's office, Chu was himself skilled at formal memorials, and so transmitted his art to him.
translations.idiomatic: At first Shangyin wrote in a lofty, archaic style of singular strangeness; in Linghu Chu's service he learned the craft of polished memorial prose, for Chu was a master of that form.

sentences.zh: 商隱儷偶長短，而繁縟過之。

translations.literal: Shangyin's parallel prose, long and short, exceeded it in ornate complexity.
translations.idiomatic: Shangyin's parallel prose, in long and short forms, surpassed his teacher's in ornate complexity.

sentences.zh: 時温庭筠、段成式倶用是相夸，號「三十六體」。

translations.literal: At the time Wen Tingyun and Duan Chengshi all used this to boast to one another, calling it the "Thirty-Six Styles."
translations.idiomatic: At the time Wen Tingyun and Duan Chengshi traded boasts in this manner, calling their manner the "Thirty-Six Styles."

sentences.zh: 薛逢薛逢字陶臣，蒲州河東人。

translations.literal: Xue Feng Xue Feng, style name Tao Chen, was a man of Hedong in Pu Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Xue Feng, courtesy name Taochen, was a native of Hedong in Pu Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 會昌初，擢進士第。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Huichang, he was raised to metropolitan graduate rank.
translations.idiomatic: In the early Huichang era he passed the metropolitan examination.

sentences.zh: 崔鉉鎭河中，表在幕府。

translations.literal: Cui Xuan commanded Hedong and listed him on a memorial in the secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: When Cui Xuan governed Hedong he appointed Feng to his staff.

sentences.zh: 鉉復宰相，引爲萬年尉。

translations.literal: When Xuan again became chief minister, he was brought in as Wannian District Captain.
translations.idiomatic: When Cui returned to the chief ministership he brought Feng in as captain of Wannian District.

sentences.zh: 直弘文館。

translations.literal: He served directly in the Hongwen Institute.
translations.idiomatic: He served on direct appointment in the Hongwen Institute.

sentences.zh: 歴侍御史、尚書郎。

translations.literal: He successively served as Attending Censor and Director in the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through the posts of attending censor and secretariat director.

sentences.zh: 持論鯁切，以謀略髙自標顯。

translations.literal: In holding discourse he was blunt and cutting; with stratagem and design he marked himself as lofty.
translations.idiomatic: His opinions were blunt and incisive; he held himself aloft as a man of strategy and design.

sentences.zh: 初，與彭城劉瑑交，瑑文辭出逢數人下，常易之。

translations.literal: Initially he associated with Liu Zuan of Pengcheng; Zuan's literary skill fell several men below Feng's, and he often treated him lightly.
translations.idiomatic: He first befriended Liu Zuan of Pengcheng, whose literary skill he ranked several notches below his own, and he often looked down on him.

sentences.zh: 瑑稍親近，逢不得意，遂相忿恨。

translations.literal: When Zuan drew somewhat close, Feng was displeased and thereupon mutual resentment arose.
translations.idiomatic: When Zuan grew somewhat close, Feng grew dissatisfied, and mutual resentment followed.

sentences.zh: 會瑑當國，有薦逢知制誥者，瑑猥言：「先朝以兩省官給事、舍人先治州縣，乃得除，逢未試州。」

translations.literal: When Zuan came to hold state power, someone recommended Feng for Drafting Edicts; Zuan basely said: "In former reigns the two-department officials as Drafting Attendants and Remonstrance Attendants first governed prefectures and districts before receiving appointment — Feng has not yet tested a prefecture."
translations.idiomatic: When Zuan came to power someone recommended Feng for drafting edicts. Zuan demeaningly objected: "Under former emperors, officials of the two secretariats had to serve in prefectural and district posts before appointment as drafting or remonstrance attendant—Feng has never held a prefectural post."

sentences.zh: 執不可。

translations.literal: He held firm and would not agree.
translations.idiomatic: He held firm and refused.

sentences.zh: 乃出爲巴州刺史。

translations.literal: Thereupon he was sent out as Prefect of Bazhou.
translations.idiomatic: Feng was instead sent out as prefect of Bazhou.

sentences.zh: 而楊收、王鐸同牒署第，收輔政，逢有詩微辭譏訕，收銜之，復斥蓬、二州刺史。

translations.literal: Yet Yang Shou and Wang Duo passed the examination in the same memorial year; Shou assisted in governance; Feng had a poem with subtle words mocking and reviling; Shou harbored resentment and again demoted him to Prefect of Peng and E Prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Shou and Wang Duo had passed the examination in the same year; when Shou came to power Feng wrote a poem with veiled mockery. Shou nursed a grudge and had him demoted again—to prefect of Pengzhou and Ezhou.

sentences.zh: 收罷，以太常少卿召還，歴給事中。

translations.literal: When Shou was removed, [Feng] was summoned back as Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and passed through Drafting Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: When Yang Shou fell from power, Feng was recalled as Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and later served as Drafting Attendant.

sentences.zh: 鐸爲宰相，逢又以詩訾鐸，鐸怒，中外亦鄙逢褊躁，故不見齒。

translations.literal: When Duo became chief minister, Feng again used a poem to censure Duo; Duo was angry, and inside and outside the court also despised Feng's narrowness and rashness, so he was not ranked among them.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Duo became chief minister, Feng again attacked him in verse. Duo was furious, and court and country alike scorned Feng's narrowness and impetuosity, so he was never fully accepted among his peers.

sentences.zh: 遷祕書監，卒。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Director of the Palace Library and died.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Director of the Palace Library and died in office.

sentences.zh: 子廷珪，進士及第。

translations.literal: His son Tinggui passed the metropolitan examination.
translations.idiomatic: His son Tinggui passed the metropolitan examination.

sentences.zh: 大順初，以司勳員外郎知制誥，遷中書舍人。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Dashun, as Outer Member of the Ministry of War he handled drafting edicts, and was promoted to Attendant Drafting at the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Dashun era he served as outer member of the Ministry of War with charge of drafting edicts, then rose to Attendant Drafting at the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 從昭宗次華州，引拜左散騎常侍，稱疾免，客成都。

translations.literal: Following Emperor Zhaozong when he halted at Hua Prefecture, he was summoned and appointed Left Regular Attendant of the Cavalry, pleaded illness to resign, and lodged as a guest at Chengdu.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Zhaozong halted at Hua Prefecture, Tinggui was appointed Left Regular Attendant of the Cavalry, pleaded illness to resign, and lived as a guest at Chengdu.

sentences.zh: 光化中，復爲舍人，累尚書左丞。

translations.literal: In the Guanghua era he again became Attendant Drafting and rose through the ranks to Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: During the Guanghua era he again became Attendant Drafting and eventually rose to Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.

sentences.zh: 朱全忠兼四鎭，廷珪以官告使至汴，客將先見，諷其拜，廷珪佯不曉，曰：「吾何德，敢受令公拜乎？」

translations.literal: Zhu Quanzhong held four circuits concurrently; Tinggui arrived at Bian as bearer of the commission patent. A guest officer saw him first and hinted that he should bow. Tinggui pretended not to understand and said, "What virtue have I that I should dare receive the Lord's bow?"
translations.idiomatic: When Zhu Quanzhong held four military circuits at once, Tinggui arrived at Bian as bearer of the commission patent. A staff officer received him first and hinted that he should bow. Tinggui feigned incomprehension and said, "What virtue have I that I should dare receive Lord Zhu's bow?

sentences.zh: 及見，卒不肯加禮。

translations.literal: When they met, to the end he would not add ceremony.
translations.idiomatic: When they met, he still refused to offer the expected courtesy.

sentences.zh: 李頻李頻字德新，睦州壽昌人。

translations.literal: Li Pin Li Pin, style name Dexin, was a man of Shouchang in Mu Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Li Pin, courtesy name Dexin, was a native of Shouchang in Mu Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 少秀悟，逮長，廬西山，多所記覽。

translations.literal: In youth he was clever and perceptive; when grown he built a hut on West Mountain and read and observed widely.
translations.idiomatic: Clever and quick-witted as a youth, he later built a hut on West Mountain and read widely.

sentences.zh: 其屬辭，於詩尤長。

translations.literal: In literary composition he was especially skilled at poetry.
translations.idiomatic: In literary composition he excelled above all in poetry.

sentences.zh: 與里人方干善。

translations.literal: He was on good terms with his townsman Fang Gan.
translations.idiomatic: He was close to his fellow townsman Fang Gan.

sentences.zh: 給事中姚合名爲詩，士多歸重，頻走千里丐其品，合大加奬挹，以女妻之。

translations.literal: Drafting Attendant Yao He was famed for poetry; scholars mostly deferred to him. Pin traveled a thousand li to beg his judgment; He greatly praised and lifted him up and gave him his daughter in marriage.
translations.idiomatic: Drafting Attendant Yao He was famed for poetry, and scholars deferred to him. Pin traveled a thousand li to seek his judgment; He praised him highly and gave him his daughter in marriage.

sentences.zh: 大中八年，擢進士第，調祕書郎，爲南陵主簿。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Dazhong he was raised to metropolitan graduate rank, assigned as Secretary, and served as Chief Clerk of Nanling.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year of the Dazhong era (854) he passed the metropolitan examination, was appointed Secretary, and served as chief clerk of Nanling.

sentences.zh: 判入等，再遷武功令。

translations.literal: His evaluation entered the top grade; he was twice promoted to Magistrate of Wugong.
translations.idiomatic: Rated in the top grade on evaluation, he was twice promoted and appointed magistrate of Wugong.

sentences.zh: 於是畿民多籍神策軍，吏以其橫，類假借，不敢繩以法。

translations.literal: At this time many people of the capital region registered under the Shence Army; officials because of their overbearing conduct mostly made loans and dared not bind them with law.
translations.idiomatic: Many residents of the capital region had registered under the Shence Army, and because those soldiers acted with impunity, officials often made concessions to them and dared not enforce the law.

sentences.zh: 頻至，有神策士尚君慶，逋賦六年不送，睅然出入閭里。

translations.literal: When Pin arrived, there was a Shence soldier Shang Junqing who for six years did not deliver overdue taxes and went in and out of the lanes with a glaring eye.
translations.idiomatic: When Pin took office, a Shence soldier named Shang Junqing had owed taxes for six years without paying and swaggered through the lanes with brazen impunity.

sentences.zh: 頻密擿比伍與競，君慶叩縣廷質，頻即械送獄，盡條宿惡，請於尹殺之，督所負無少貸。

translations.literal: Pin secretly pressed the mutual-responsibility groups to compete; Junqing came to the county court to dispute; Pin immediately shackled him and sent him to prison, fully listed his old crimes, and asked the metropolitan magistrate to execute him, pressing what was owed without the least remission.
translations.idiomatic: Pin secretly urged the mutual-responsibility groups to press the case. Junqing came to the county court to dispute the matter; Pin immediately had him shackled and sent to prison, listed all his past offenses, and asked the metropolitan magistrate to execute him, collecting every penny owed without remission.

sentences.zh: 豪猾大驚，屛息奉法，縣大治。

translations.literal: The powerful and crafty were greatly alarmed, held their breath and obeyed the law, and the county was greatly well governed.
translations.idiomatic: The powerful and unscrupulous were terrified into obedience, and the county was brought to excellent order.

sentences.zh: 有六門堰者，廞廢百五十年，方歳饑，頻發官廥庸民浚渠，按故道廝水溉田，穀以大稔。

translations.literal: There was the Six Gates Weir, abandoned for a hundred and fifty years; just then there was famine. Pin opened the official granaries and hired the people to dredge the canal, followed the old course to divide the water and irrigate the fields, and grain was greatly abundant.
translations.idiomatic: The Six Gates Weir had lain abandoned for a hundred and fifty years. During a famine Pin opened the official granaries and hired laborers to dredge the canal, restored the old watercourse to irrigate the fields, and the harvest was abundant.

sentences.zh: 懿宗嘉之，賜緋衣、銀魚。

translations.literal: Emperor Yizong commended him and bestowed crimson robes and a silver fish tally.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Yizong commended him and bestowed crimson robes and a silver fish tally.

sentences.zh: 俄擢侍御史，守法不阿徇，遷累都官員外郎。

translations.literal: Soon he was promoted to Attending Censor, upheld the law without bending or favoring, and rose through the ranks to Outer Member of the Ministry of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was promoted to Attending Censor, upheld the law without favoritism, and rose to Outer Member of the Ministry of Justice.

sentences.zh: 表丐建州刺史。

translations.literal: He memorialized begging for Prefect of Jian Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He petitioned to be appointed prefect of Jianzhou.

sentences.zh: 既至，以禮法治下，更布條教。

translations.literal: Once he arrived, he governed subordinates with ritual and law and issued new regulations.
translations.idiomatic: Once there, he governed through ritual and law and issued new regulations.

sentences.zh: 時朝政亂，盜興，相椎奪，而建賴頻以安。

translations.literal: At the time court governance was chaotic, bandits arose, and they seized from one another, yet Jian relied on Pin and was secure.
translations.idiomatic: Court governance was chaotic, banditry flourished, and rivals seized one another's territory, yet Jian remained secure thanks to Pin.

sentences.zh: 卒官下，喪歸，父老相與扶柩，葬永樂州，爲立廟梨山，歳祠之。

translations.literal: He died in office; when the coffin returned, the elders together supported the bier, buried him in Yongle Prefecture, and built a temple for him on Pear Mountain, sacrificing to him every year.
translations.idiomatic: He died in office. When his coffin was borne home, the elders together supported the bier. He was buried in Yongle Prefecture, and a temple was built for him on Pear Mountain, where he was honored with annual sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 天下亂，盜發其冢，壽昌人隨加封掩云。

translations.literal: When the realm fell into disorder, bandits opened his tomb; the people of Shouchang promptly added sealing and covering.
translations.idiomatic: When the empire fell into chaos, bandits opened his tomb, and the people of Shouchang promptly resealed it.

sentences.zh: 呉融呉融字子華，越州山陰人。

translations.literal: Wu Rong Wu Rong, style name Zihua, was a man of Shanyin in Yue Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Rong, courtesy name Zihua, was a native of Shanyin in Yue Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 祖翥，有名大中時，觀察府召以署吏，不應，帥髙其概，言諸朝，賜號文簡先生。

translations.literal: His grandfather Zhu was famed in the Dazhong era; the observation office summoned him to sign on as clerk; he did not respond; the commander esteemed his integrity, spoke of him at court, and bestowed the title Master Wenjian.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Zhu was renowned in the Dazhong era. The observation commission summoned him to serve as a clerk, but he refused. The governor admired his integrity, recommended him at court, and the throne granted him the title Master Wenjian.

sentences.zh: 融學自力，富辭調。

translations.literal: Rong studied through his own effort and was rich in literary tone.
translations.idiomatic: Rong studied through his own effort and was richly gifted in literary expression.

sentences.zh: 龍紀初，及進士第。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Longji he passed the metropolitan examination.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Longji era he passed the metropolitan examination.

sentences.zh: 韋昭度討蜀，表掌書記，遷累侍御史。

translations.literal: When Wei Zhaodu campaigned against Shu, he listed him on a memorial as chief recorder and he rose through the ranks to Attending Censor.
translations.idiomatic: When Wei Zhaodu campaigned against Shu, he appointed Rong chief recorder on his staff, and Rong rose to Attending Censor.

sentences.zh: 坐累去官，流浪荊南，依成汭。

translations.literal: Because of an entangling offense he left office, wandered in Jingnan, and relied on Cheng Rui.
translations.idiomatic: After an entangling offense cost him his post, he wandered in Jingnan and found refuge with Cheng Rui.

sentences.zh: 久之，召爲左補闕，以禮部郎中爲翰林學士，拜中書舍人。

translations.literal: After a long time he was summoned as Left Remonstrator, served as Hanlin Academician with the title of Director in the Ministry of Rites, and was appointed Attendant Drafting at the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: After a long interval he was summoned as Left Remonstrator, entered the Hanlin as academician while holding the post of Director in the Ministry of Rites, and was appointed Attendant Drafting at the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 昭宗反正，御南闕，臣稱賀，融最先至。

translations.literal: When Emperor Zhaozong was restored, he took the southern gate; ministers offered congratulations; Rong arrived first.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Zhaozong was restored to the throne and appeared at the southern gate, the ministers offered congratulations, and Rong was the first to arrive.

sentences.zh: 于時左右歡駭，帝有指授，疊十許稿，融跪作詔，少選成，語當意詳，帝咨賞良厚。

translations.literal: At that time those left and right were joyous and startled; the Emperor gave instructions; more than ten drafts were stacked; Rong knelt and composed the edict; in a short while it was finished, the language fitting the intent and detailed; the Emperor consulted and rewarded him very generously.
translations.idiomatic: The courtiers were overjoyed and astonished. The emperor gave instructions, and more than ten drafts were prepared. Rong knelt and composed the edict; in a short while it was finished, its language fitting the intent and full in detail. The emperor praised and rewarded him generously.

sentences.zh: 進戸部侍郎。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Vice Minister of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Vice Minister of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 鳳翔劫遷，融不克從，去客閿鄕。

translations.literal: When Fengxiang seized the emperor in forced removal, Rong could not follow and left to lodge as a guest at Wen Township.
translations.idiomatic: When the Fengxiang faction seized the emperor and forced his removal, Rong could not follow and withdrew to lodge as a guest at Wen Township.

sentences.zh: 俄召還翰林，遷承旨，卒官。

translations.literal: Soon he was summoned back to the Hanlin, promoted to Chief Academician, and died in office.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was recalled to the Hanlin, promoted to Chief Academician, and died in office.
